articles.title: Steam tiene gratis estos 6 juegos para PC: cómo descargarlos
articles.text:
Steam agregó seis juegos gratis para PC con Windows: Incident Archives: Flight 882, Relyora, Vice Signalling, DreamNet y Eclipsia.
Para acceder a ellos, hay que ingresar a Steam desde la app para Windows o desde el navegador, buscar cada título en la tienda y presionar el botón “Free to Play” (gratis para jugar) para sumarlos a la biblioteca.
PUBLICIDAD
De qué trata cada uno de los juegos nuevos
- Incident Archives: Flight 882.
Una experiencia corta, de unos 20 minutos, inspirada en hechos reales. El jugador se convierte en un nuevo capitán durante un vuelo nocturno y lo que empieza como un viaje normal se vuelve inquietante a medida que la tensión crece.
- Relyora.
Un RPG roguelite de fantasía oscura con progresión incremental. Permite elegir una especialización, enfrentar jefes poderosos, recolectar artefactos y convertir cada partida en poder permanente antes de desafiar el “Infinite Dungeon”.
PUBLICIDAD
- Vice Signalling.
Un juego narrativo corto en el que el jugador se infiltra en una sociedad secreta de ricos y poderosos. La propuesta se centra en descifrar señales secretas y usarlas para descubrir una conspiración contra el Emperador.
- DreamNet.
Un juego de exploración “Frutiger Aero” free-to-play que invita a redescubrir el internet de los años 2000. Propone sumergirse en mundos nostálgicos, descubrir su historia y revivir la estética de la “vieja web”.
PUBLICIDAD
- Eclipsia.
Un RPG idle free-to-play en el que hay que construir un equipo de héroes únicos, derrotar jefes, reunir botín legendario y crecer con progresión constante. Incluye descubrimiento de equipamiento raro, optimización de builds y una aventura en un mundo de fantasía en expansión.

articles.title: TikTok Agrees to $400 Million Settlement in U.S. Child Privacy Lawsuit
articles.text:
The U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) announced on Friday that ByteDance-owned TikTok will pay $400 million to settle a 2024 lawsuit accusing the company of violating child privacy laws in the country.
As part of the settlement, the social media platform will pay $300 million immediately, and an additional $100 million "upon entry of an order vacating a prior consent decree entered against TikTok’s predecessor, Musical.ly," the DoJ said in a press release.
A complaint filed back in August 2024 alongside the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) accused the company of "massive-scale invasions of children's privacy" by knowingly allowing children under 13 to create TikTok accounts and unlawfully collecting data from those who used it in "Kids Mode."
It further alleged TikTok and its parent company ByteDance failed to "comply with parents' requests to delete their children's accounts and information."
At the time, the company disputed the arguments, stating many of them related to "past events and practices" that were either "factually inaccurate or have been addressed."
The DoJ characterized the settlement as "one of the largest recoveries ever" obtained in connection with U.S. federal child privacy law, also referred to as the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA).
It also noted that the tech company has since implemented extensive measures to improve safeguards for younger users, strengthen age-related controls, and improve parental oversight.
"This settlement is a major victory for American children and parents," said Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward Jr.
"The Department's priority is ensuring that children are protected online and that companies entrusted with their personal information meet their legal obligations. This resolution secures a substantial recovery while reinforcing the protections that families expect and deserve."
This is not the first time TikTok has landed in regulatory crosshairs over child data privacy. In September 2023, TikTok was levied a €345 million fine for violating the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) in relation to its processing of children’s personal data.
Earlier this year, a U.S. joint venture allowed the app to continue operating in the country without a ban in accordance with a divest-or-ban law upheld by the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Nintendo elimina más de 400 emuladores de Switch de GitHub en 24 horas
articles.text:
Nintendo eliminó más de 400 repositorios vinculados a emuladores de Nintendo Switch en GitHub en un lapso de 24 horas, en una nueva ofensiva legal con reclamos por derechos de autor.
La medida se enmarca en la estrategia de la compañía para frenar la piratería y bloquear el acceso a herramientas que permiten ejecutar juegos de la consola sin comprarlos.
PUBLICIDAD
La ola de bajas llegó después de acciones similares en los últimos años: en mayo de 2024, Nintendo ya había impulsado la eliminación de más de ocho mil versiones del emulador Yuzu con un aviso legal enviado a GitHub, y en febrero de 2026 volvió a pedir que se retiraran los archivos que aún quedaban de ese proyecto, además de los vinculados a otros 12 sistemas.
Qué hizo Nintendo
Nintendo envió siete avisos en un solo día para solicitar la baja de repositorios que alojaban o enlazaban código asociado a emuladores de Nintendo Switch.
PUBLICIDAD
El resultado fue la eliminación de 401 repositorios, con un impacto concentrado en Suyu, que perdió 311 de esos espacios.
Entre los proyectos mencionados también figuraron Skyline, un sistema para celulares Android, y MonoNX, un programa creado en lenguaje C#, además de múltiples variantes que tomaban como base el código de Yuzu.
PUBLICIDAD
En los repositorios afectados, al intentar ingresar hoy aparece un mensaje que indica que el contenido fue retirado e incluye un enlace al reclamo presentado por Nintendo.
En su argumentación, la empresa sostuvo que estos repositorios “ofrecen, enlazan o proporcionan de otro modo acceso a emuladores de Nintendo Switch” y que esos emuladores “están diseñados principalmente para jugar juegos de Nintendo Switch”.
PUBLICIDAD
En ese marco, afirmó que “eluden ilegalmente los TPMs de Nintendo” para ejecutar copias ilegales de juegos.
Nintendo también detalló aspectos técnicos de su postura: indicó que “los juegos de Nintendo Switch están encriptados mediante claves criptográficas patentadas (prod.keys)” y concluyó que, durante el funcionamiento, los emuladores “utilizan necesariamente copias no autorizadas de estas claves criptográficas” para desencriptar copias no autorizadas de juegos (ROMs), sin autorización de la compañía.
PUBLICIDAD
El texto del aviso cerró con el argumento de que la distribución de estos emuladores constituiría “un tráfico ilícito” según la DMCA.
Qué es GitHub y qué son los emuladores
GitHub es una plataforma que permite alojar y administrar repositorios de código, es decir, “espacios” donde se guarda software y su historial de cambios, y que además facilita la colaboración entre desarrolladores.
PUBLICIDAD
En este caso, los repositorios señalados por Nintendo funcionaban como puntos de distribución o acceso a herramientas asociadas a emulación.
Los emuladores, en términos generales, son programas que buscan replicar el funcionamiento de una consola en otro dispositivo para poder ejecutar sus juegos.
En el caso citado, el reclamo de Nintendo apuntó a repositorios que, según la compañía, permitían jugar títulos de Nintendo Switch sin pagar y que, además, eludían medidas tecnológicas de protección, apoyándose en claves criptográficas mencionadas en el propio aviso.
PUBLICIDAD
Nintendo ofrece gratis No Man’s Sky
No Man’s Sky puede jugarse sin costo extra para quienes tengan una suscripción activa a Nintendo Switch Online, gracias a su inclusión como “juego de muestra”, una modalidad que habilita el acceso al título completo por un período limitado.
Nintendo España señaló además que, mediante un paquete de mejora gratuito, los usuarios también podrán probar el juego “optimizado en Nintendo Switch 2”.
Se trata de un videojuego de ciencia ficción enfocado en la exploración y la supervivencia dentro de un universo “infinito” generado de manera procedimental. La propuesta ofrece una galaxia abierta, con planetas y formas de vida diferentes, y permite pasar del espacio a la superficie “sin pantallas de carga y sin límites”, de acuerdo con su descripción oficial.
PUBLICIDAD
El avance puede encararse por distintas vías —combate, comercio o exploración— según las decisiones del jugador, con opciones para mejorar la nave, el arma y el traje, y así adaptarse a condiciones ambientales hostiles.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Korean engineers are now turning to the deep blue sea for data centers
articles.text:
South Korean city bets on the ocean to solve its AI data center crisis — but this is only the beginning
A small Korean coastal city could soon host up to 100,000 AI servers
- Ulsan is testing underwater data centers to support growing AI workloads
- The project carries a KRW 51.1 billion (about $37 million) budget through 2030
- Seawater could provide cooling without conventional mechanical refrigeration systems
South Korean city Ulsan is exploring underwater infrastructure as AI computing continues to strain land availability, power grids, and cooling systems nationwide.
The city is partnering with the Korea Institute of Ocean Science and Technology (KIOST) to design a standardized subsea data center model.
Officials hope the approach can ease some of the site and cooling constraints that conventional data centers increasingly face across the country.
Building a standardized underwater model
The partnership between Ulsan and KIOST runs through 2030, with a combined budget of KRW 51.1 billion (about $37 million) - KRW 40 billion (about $29 million) of which comes directly from the central government, with the remainder covered locally.
“Ulsan plans to complete the standard model by 2030 and begin developing an underwater data-center complex for commercialization from 2031,” the city said.
The goal is a working, carbon-neutral template for underwater computing that other sites could later replicate.
The project will take place in waters roughly 20 meters deep off the Ulsan coastline, where engineers plan to rely on seawater — which averages about 13.3°C annually — as a core part of the cooling strategy.

Researchers intend to combine pressure-resistant vessel design with hybrid cooling systems described as ultra-high-efficiency by project planners.
Server units and power distribution equipment will follow standardized modular designs meant to simplify future scaling.
The team is aiming for an operating efficiency of approximately PUE 1.2 once testing concludes.
SK Telecom joined the partnership in January 2026, taking on responsibility for GPU-based infrastructure and server operations management.
In addition to Ulsan and KIOST, other research organizations, academics and industry professionals are part of the project working behind the scenes.
Their combined role covers everything from vessel engineering to the software layer that will eventually manage AI workloads underwater.
A larger commercial vision
A separate, longer-term concept discussed by the city involves roughly KRW 500 billion (about $360 million) in investment and capacity for up to 100,000 servers.
This larger sum is not tied to the current phase of work and only reflects what a full commercial buildout could eventually cost.
Whether Ulsan reaches that scale will depend entirely on how the initial testing phase performs.
South Korea faces mounting pressure to expand computing capacity as AI workloads multiply across chipmakers, cloud providers, and research institutions nationwide.
Land near major population centers remains scarce and expensive, pushing planners toward unconventional sites away from crowded urban areas.
Ocean water offers a cooling resource that requires none of the mechanical refrigeration conventional facilities depend on heavily.
If the Ulsan demonstration performs as expected, similar underwater sites could eventually spread along other stretches of Korea's coastline.
For now, the ocean floor represents a promising but unproven answer to Korea's expanding AI infrastructure demands.

articles.title: Sony revela su nuevo plan para PlayStation y deja en segundo plano las ventas de PS5
articles.text:
Sony ha decidido cambiar el foco de su estrategia con PlayStation. La compañía ya no busca aumentar de forma agresiva las ventas de la PS5 durante la segunda mitad de su ciclo de vida y pretende concentrarse en obtener más ingresos de los jugadores que ya forman parte de su ecosistema.
La decisión fue explicada por Hiroki Totoki, presidente de Sony, quien señaló en una entrevista con The Wall Street Journal que el aumento de los precios de algunos componentes coincide con una etapa en la que la compañía ya no necesita impulsar las ventas de la consola a cualquier precio.
PUBLICIDAD
La PS5 ha superado los 95 millones de unidades vendidas, una cifra que coloca a la actual generación en una posición consolidada. Ante este escenario, Sony considera que tiene más sentido aprovechar la enorme base de usuarios existente que intentar atraer nuevos compradores mediante una estrategia centrada exclusivamente en el hardware.
Sony quiere sacar más rendimiento a sus jugadores
El cambio de rumbo supone que PlayStation tendrá que depender cada vez más de los ingresos generados después de la venta de una consola. Entre las áreas que cobran mayor importancia se encuentran las suscripciones, las compras digitales, las microtransacciones y los videojuegos que incorporan servicios adicionales.
PUBLICIDAD
Totoki también destacó que PlayStation cuenta con alrededor de 125 millones de usuarios activos mensuales. Esta cifra representa un mercado considerable para Sony, ya que permite generar ingresos de forma recurrente sin necesidad de que cada usuario compre una nueva consola.
La estrategia consiste, por tanto, en mantener activa a esa comunidad y conseguir que continúe gastando dentro del ecosistema PlayStation. Una persona que ya tiene una PS5 puede generar ingresos mediante la compra de juegos digitales, contenido adicional, servicios de suscripción o transacciones dentro de determinados títulos.
PUBLICIDAD
Este modelo también reduce la dependencia de los ingresos obtenidos exclusivamente por la venta inicial de la consola.
El aumento del precio de los componentes cambia el escenario
El contexto económico también ha influido en la decisión. Totoki explicó que el incremento del coste de determinados componentes tecnológicos está afectando a la industria y señaló especialmente la situación del mercado de la memoria.
PUBLICIDAD
Para Sony, el momento resulta favorable porque la PS5 ya se encuentra en la segunda mitad de su ciclo de vida. En estas circunstancias, la compañía puede reducir la presión por incrementar las ventas de hardware mientras concentra sus esfuerzos en otras fuentes de ingresos.
La situación contrasta con los primeros años de una generación de consolas, cuando los fabricantes necesitan construir rápidamente una base instalada suficientemente grande para atraer desarrolladores y crear un ecosistema competitivo.
PUBLICIDAD
En el caso de PS5, Sony ya cuenta con una comunidad de millones de jugadores y una amplia oferta de videojuegos y servicios.
La PS6 podría enfrentarse a un escenario diferente
El cambio de estrategia también plantea dudas sobre la próxima generación de PlayStation. Si los costes de componentes continúan elevados cuando llegue la PS6, Sony podría encontrarse con mayores dificultades para mantener un precio competitivo.
PUBLICIDAD
Los analistas consideran que el contexto actual puede beneficiar a la PS5 porque la compañía ya no necesita venderla de forma agresiva. Sin embargo, una futura consola tendría que afrontar nuevamente el desafío de justificar su precio y convencer a los consumidores para actualizar su hardware.
Por ahora, Sony parece apostar por otro camino: aprovechar al máximo los 125 millones de usuarios activos mensuales que ya tiene PlayStation y convertir esa enorme comunidad en una fuente de ingresos recurrentes.
PUBLICIDAD
La estrategia marca un cambio importante en la forma de medir el éxito de una consola. Para Sony, vender millones de PS5 seguirá siendo relevante, pero cada vez tendrá más peso lo que hagan los jugadores después de comprarla.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: GTA 6's Netflix timed exclusive for its extended look is egregious, with no benefit for consumers — and there's no reason to be defending it
articles.text:
GTA 6's Netflix timed exclusive, and gamers' defense of it sums up why the gaming industry is as bad as it is today
This is how anti-consumer practices begin
The wait for perhaps the most anticipated game of all time, Grand Theft Auto 6, has spanned just over a decade since its developer, Rockstar Games, released the last entry in the series. Its 2023 reveal convinced fans it would arrive sooner than expected — but multiple delays sapped plenty of the excitement.
After years of anticipation, GTA 6 is finally almost here, set to launch on November 19, 2026, on PS5, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S, with no delays in sight. The hype levels are increasing yet again, and it's undoubtedly an exciting time for the gaming industry.
Unfortunately, the build-up to launch has recently been marred not only by Sony pioneering the end of physical game discs, but also by Rockstar's anti-consumer shenanigans during GTA 6's dull marketing campaign — starting with the announcement of no physical copy.
In case you missed it, an extended look at GTA 6 will be available on August 27, 2026, on Netflix as a 6-hour exclusive, before being published by Rockstar on YouTube (and presumably other platforms). In other words, if you want to see what Rockstar has to offer firsthand and at the earliest available opportunity, you'll need to pay for a Netflix subscription.
Now, I'm not a spokesperson for gamers, but I'm sure I'm not the only one who quite literally sees this as a way for Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive (its parent company) to kickstart paid trailers — and the reactions online are a very worrying indication of a potential new precedent.
Stop defending anti-consumer practices
Here's the thing: you can still be excited about what is arguably the biggest game of all time, and still criticize a developer or publisher for justified reasons. I think it goes without saying that Rockstar's Netflix exclusivity deal is one of those reasons.
Locking a game trailer or gameplay showcase behind a paywall, even if it is just half an hour, is a massive red flag for any video game company, in my view. This is an unprecedented situation where fans are the ones paying to view marketing material, the same material that would previously be free to consume at the moment it was published.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
My main concern comes from the reaction online; many gamers are effectively defending the exclusivity deal, with typical statements such as "you're only complaining because you're broke" or "it's not that big of a deal, it's just 6 hours".
Neither the price nor the amount of time of exclusivity matters, but rather, it's the principle and what foundation Rockstar and Netflix's move could mean for the future. It feels like Rockstar is testing the waters to see how consumers respond, and frankly, is taking advantage of gamers' fear of missing out and the desperation to see something new in GTA 6.
There's absolutely no benefit to the timed exclusive being locked behind a paywall for consumers, and it's actually quite surprising to see many come to Rockstar's defense.
I can't help but feel like if this were any other game studio (i.e., Ubisoft) pulling this exact move, the uproar and backlash would be as loud as ever. I'm well aware that GTA 6 is a significantly bigger game than any in this generation, but that doesn't suddenly mean we should gloss over anti-consumer practices.
This same attitude of "it's not that expensive" or "stop moaning" was widespread when the video game price standard was raised to $70 — and now, edging closer to $80 thanks to Mario Kart World and GTA 6.
Long before that, services like Sony's PlayStation Plus and Microsoft's Xbox Live quickly became normalized, stripping away free online multiplayer access. Gamers overlooked that, likely due to the benefits of 'free' monthly games, and now there's no going back.
That same concept is being applied here: if Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar, Netflix, and possibly other game publishers notice a massive influx of Netflix subscribers for GTA 6's extended look, there's a decent chance early access to game trailers will gradually become the new normal.
It will indirectly tell publishers that consumers are okay with paying for marketing material, out of pure excitement, which is to be expected for a game as big as GTA 6. Isn't that ugly?
This entire case explains why the gaming industry is in the state that it's in today. Gamers accept, or rather, minimize far too many anti-consumer practices by corporations before it's too late for them to backtrack, and we're seeing it unfold yet again.
I'm not saying gamers shouldn't buy GTA 6, even if you're against Rockstar not providing a game disc and protesting against Sony's decision. GTA 6 is the only game that I and many others won't skip out on, as the wait for the experience has been monumental, and that's okay.
However, that doesn't mean you can't still protest against the axing of true physical game copies and call out Netflix's timed exclusivity as a step too far, especially since the full experience of GTA 6 already costs $100 via the controversial ultimate edition.
Gamers need to realize that consumers hold the power overall, as banding together against unpopular practices can lead to change — but sadly, I think many fans will continue to look past Rockstar and Netflix's actions, simply because of their excitement, and that's a shame.

articles.title: XSquare raises pre-Seed round to expand into Saudi Arabia
articles.text: UAE-based fintech XSquare has raised an undisclosed pre-Seed round. The round saw participation from Raed Ventures, AngelSpark, 500 Global and Oraseya Capital, the venture capital arm of Dubai Integrated Economic Zones. Founded in 2023 by Tanvir Shah and Ashwin Shenoy, XSquare is building a B2B payment orchestration platform that brings multiple payment rails, collections, payments and reconciliation into a single system for businesses. XSquare is currently live in the UAE and Qatar, with its Qatar launch marking its first cross-border expansion. The funding will be used to expand XSquare’s payment rail and banking partnerships, grow its engineering and commercial teams, and launch operations in Saudi Arabia. Earlier this year, XSquare raised a funding round from AngelSpark for an undisclosed value. Press release: XSquare, a business-to-business (B2B) payments company operating in partnership with Mastercard, today announced the successful close of its Pre-Seed funding round. The round had participation from Raed Ventures, AngelSpark, 500 Global and Oraseya Capital, the venture capital arm of Dubai Integrated Economic Zones. With the new capital, XSquare is scaling what it describes as the region's first and only payment orchestration layer built purely for B2B. The platform unifies multiple payment rails behind a single integration, allowing businesses to collect, pay and reconcile across providers without stitching together separate systems. XSquare is launching with rails from Telr, Geidea, VaultsPay, Spare and Tess Payments, with further partners to follow. Under its partnership with Mastercard, the company is also bringing Mastercard's B2B payments product to market, enabling card-funded supplier and vendor payments that settle directly to bank accounts. XSquare is deploying the program with marquee government and large corporate clients, unlocking commercial card economics on business spend that has traditionally sat outside the card ecosystem. Beyond its UAE base, XSquare is live in Qatar, where it holds a presence at the Qatar Financial Centre (QFC) and is partnering with leading banks and regulated payment partners in Doha. The Qatar launch marks the company’s first cross-border expansion and lays the groundwork for a wider GCC footprint. “B2B payments in this region have been underserved for too long, forced onto tools built for consumer markets. We are building the payment infrastructure that regional businesses need: card and bank rails, orchestration and reconciliation, all in one place. Having Raed Ventures, AngelSpark, 500 Global and Oraseya Capital participate in this round is a strong endorsement of that vision and of the traction we are seeing with Banks, Government entities and large Corporates.” Tanvir Shah, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer, XSquare “We like to back companies that build enabling infrastructure for the region’s digital economy and are led by teams with strong founder-market fit. XSquare is building critical infrastructure for the largely underserved B2B payments market, and Tanvir and Ashwin have the experience and relationships required to build and scale in this market. We’re excited to back them and look forward to supporting their expansion across the region.” Saed Nashef, Founding Partner, Raed Ventures XSquare plans to use the funding to expand its rail and bank partnerships, grow its engineering and commercial teams, and begin operations in Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Betty La Fea: Más Fea Que Nunca en Prime Video: entrevista exclusiva con Betty, Don Armando y el regreso de Michel
articles.text:
Infobae Tecno entrevistó en exclusiva a Ana María Orozco, Jorge Enrique Abello y Patrick Delmas por el lanzamiento de “Betty, la fea: más fea que nunca”, el título de la tercera temporada de la reconocida telenovela colombiana.
La serie estrena esta nueva entrega el 28 de agosto de 2026 en Amazon Prime Video. Durante la conversación, los actores compartieron sus sensaciones sobre el regreso, las transformaciones de sus personajes y la experiencia de reencontrarse en el set después de tantos años.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, hubo espacio dejar volar la creatividad con sus personajes. Por ejemplo, Jorge Enrique Abello eligió “Strangers in the Night” de Frank Sinatra como la canción que Armando habría escogido para bailar con Betty desde el principio, subrayando la diferencia entre ambos personajes.
Ana María Orozco imaginó que Betty conquistaría a Armando con una nota secreta y a Michel invitándolo a tomar jugo de mora, una bebida muy popular en Colombia y que se menciona muchas veces en la telenovela.
PUBLICIDAD
La tercera temporada se estrenará en la plataforma el 28 de agosto - crédito Prime Video
Patrick Delmas, como Michel, eligió a Dora Cadavid (Inesita) como la integrante del cuartel de las feas a la que invitaría a tomar un té y conversar sobre la cultura del país.
Cómo vivieron el reencuentro en el set los personajes de Betty, la fea
Ana María Orozco expresó su agradecimiento y alegría por volver a interpretar a Betty, resaltando la importancia de trabajar con un elenco y equipo que considera “maravilloso”.
PUBLICIDAD
“Me siento muy afortunada del regalo que me ha dado la vida de interpretar a Betty, de tener además estos compañeros y este equipo. En estas nuevas temporadas se ha conformado un equipo comprometido con la historia”, afirmó.
Jorge Enrique Abello subrayó la complicidad entre los protagonistas. “Los tres siempre hemos disfrutado mucho ese pedacito de la historia. Cada vez que nos juntamos para hacer ese pedacito de Betty es algo que nos alegra muchísimo. Hay alegría ahí, la palabra”, aseguró.
PUBLICIDAD
Patrick Delmas describió el proceso como “una delicia” y valoró especialmente el trabajo del director Juan Carlos Mazo, quien ha dotado a la producción de un nuevo espíritu.
Qué cambió en la preparación de los personajes
En cuanto a la preparación de los personajes, Delmas confesó que en los inicios de la serie (hace más de 20 años) no hubo una preparación formal y que muchas escenas surgieron desde la improvisación y la complicidad entre el elenco.
PUBLICIDAD
En la nueva etapa, el reencuentro y el trabajo con el nuevo equipo creativo han aportado un enfoque coral y teatral.
Ana María Orozco reflexionó sobre la evolución de Betty y su propio aprendizaje como actriz.
“Nunca juzgo nada, me pongo al servicio de lo que le pase a ella. Me gusta que Betty se cuestione cosas, que se muestre vulnerable. No es alguien que tiene todo resuelto ni que da lecciones. Eso la hace más humana y cercana”, señaló.
PUBLICIDAD
Jorge Enrique Abello abordó la transformación de la masculinidad de Armando Mendoza: “La masculinidad en la cual está fundamentada la personalidad de Armando pertenece a un mundo que ya no existe. Armando apenas está comprendiendo eso y es un choque para él. Ahora vive un verdadero infierno”, dijo.
De qué trata Betty, la fea: más fea que nunca
“Betty, la fea: más fea que nunca” es la tercera temporada de la emblemática telenovela colombiana. La trama arranca en Bogotá, donde Betty asiste al desfile de despedida de Hugo Lombardi y se reencuentra con el Cuartel de las Feas.

Betty atraviesa un proceso de transformación personal, inicia terapia, se independiza y enfrenta una crisis en Ecomoda tras un escándalo de plagio. Además, revive un triángulo amoroso entre Armando y Michel, su expareja francesa, lo que reabre conflictos emocionales y profesionales

articles.title: Hearing what Trinnov's elite AV processor can do with 3D room correction made me rethink my own home theater system in a big way
articles.text:
How Trinnov's Altitude CI AV processor showed me the importance of flagship 3D room correction in elite home cinema setups
And somehow, it managed to do it in an elevator lobby
I want to tell you about the Trinnov Altitude CI AV processor. And I want to tell you about it because it’s essentially an Intel computer posing as a processor with scalable channels and a software-based platform that is constantly being updated.
But I need to tell you about how Trinnov was able to make a pair of ASCENDO Black Swan speakers sound good in what was essentially an elevator lobby, at Audio Advice Live 2026.
The Black Swan Active Ext speakers are excellent two-way speakers that can get loud with a 132dB peak. They even come with their own DSP. After all, the ones showcased at the event, which were in a custom finish, retail around for around $40,000 each (so around £29,550 / AU$ 56,200) and there’s more going on than just an asymmetrical horn. It’s also worth mentioning that a $36,000 ASCENDO subwoofer was in the mix as well.
It’s not ASCENDO’s DSP doing the work in this particular situation though, it’s the Trinnov Altitude CI. Using Trinnov’s unique and patented Waveforming and Optimizer technology — there’s also a 3D mic for getting measurements — the audio, whether it was Stevie Ray Vaughn, Kamasi Washington (I did get a request in), or even some EDM, was as pristine and clear across all frequencies as if I were listening in a dedicated room.
Now, I’m describing the sound within about ten feet of the speakers where some seating had been set up to appreciate all that was on offer. It did start to get a little diffuse when over by registration, about thirty feet to the right, or at the elevators, thirty feet back, but those were not intended listening areas. The ability and fine tuning of Trinnov’s DSP is hard to beat.
Can you imagine creating a listenable space in a room with high-arched ceilings, walkways in either direction and a wall of elevators on the far end? Now, imagine what the Trinnov Altitude CI can do in a more ideal space.
The Room Correction
There are a few things going on with the Trinnov Altitude CI (and really and of the Altitude series) that get the room out of the equation and allow a set of speakers to sing. One of the main components of the company’s renowned room correction is its patented Optimizer, which, using a 3D mic, takes accurate measurements of what the room is hearing and adjusts accordingly. You can even do vertical and horizontal adjustments via the software to compensate for non-ideal speaker placement.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Trinnov also has its Waveforming technology, introduced in 2023 when researching a way to prevent standing waves instead of fixing them. Speaker and subwoofer placement as well as EQ were the traditional way of trying to mitigate the effects of standing waves, but you still get cold and hot spots throughout the room. And unless you only want to listen to music by yourself — this is less important for that one seat situated in the sweet spot — you would want to get rid of those standing waves as much as possible.
By implementing Waveforming, you get much better seat-to-seat consistency. And you’ll remove the muddiness from the low-end for a clearer sound and more dynamic contrast (there’s usually a standing wave around 50Hz). It also surprisingly makes dialogue easier to hear if you’re using the Trinnov Altitude CI for a Home Theater setting as well (or listening to a podcast through your Hi-Fi speakers for some reason).
Looking under the hood
Earlier I called the Trinnov Altitude CI an Intel computer, and it’s true. It uses an actual CPU and has a heavily modified Linux base for its software. What this means is that Trinnov doesn’t have to wait for someone to make a special DSP chip for them to build around as the internal processor is more than powerful enough. And that by making the processing software-based, the company can roll out any updates to Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, Dante, or anything else with a software update that just requires a press of a button and a few minutes.
This means that if you own any Trinnov AV processor, they will stay up to date for the foreseeable future so you won’t need to go replacing hardware every time there’s something new under the sun.
On the hardware side, the only moving target these days is HDMI. With the Trinnov Altitude CI, the HDMI ports are all separated on their own piece of hardware that can be removed for an updated one that you would get from the company so that your processor can support the new standard. Beats buying a whole new AV processor.
The one thing that really sets the Trinnov Altitude CI apart from the Altitude 16 or 32 is that it has scalable channels. So when you purchase this processor, it includes eight channels in that initial price tag of about $12,000 / £8,870 / AU$16,960 and you can add channels two at a time after until you get to 32 channels, and it’s about $28,000 / £20,700 / AU$39,560 for the Altitude CI fully loaded. You’ll have to reach out to your local Hi-Fi dealer for exact pricing, but the Trinnov Altitude CI offers a more affordable entry point into the Trinnov ecosystem.

articles.title: Qué ocurre con tus datos cuando desinstalas una aplicación del celular
articles.text:
Desinstalar una aplicación del celular no significa que toda la información relacionada con ella desaparezca. Al eliminar el programa, el teléfono borra los archivos necesarios para ejecutarlo y, dependiendo del sistema y de la aplicación, parte de los datos almacenados localmente.
Sin embargo, la cuenta del usuario, las fotografías, los mensajes y otros contenidos guardados en los servidores del servicio pueden permanecer intactos.
La diferencia es importante porque muchas aplicaciones actuales funcionan conectadas a una cuenta. En estos casos, el programa instalado en el teléfono es apenas una puerta de acceso a información que puede estar almacenada en internet. Por eso, eliminar una app no equivale a cerrar una cuenta ni a solicitar que una compañía borre nuestros datos.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué elimina realmente el teléfono
Cuando un usuario desinstala una aplicación, tanto Android como iPhone eliminan el programa del dispositivo. También pueden desaparecer determinados datos locales que la aplicación utilizaba para funcionar, como configuraciones, archivos temporales o información almacenada directamente en el almacenamiento interno.
Esto permite recuperar parte del espacio ocupado por la aplicación. Sin embargo, lo que ocurre con los demás archivos depende de cómo haya sido diseñada cada plataforma.
PUBLICIDAD
Por ejemplo, una aplicación puede guardar fotografías, vídeos o documentos en carpetas independientes del sistema. En esos casos, esos archivos personales pueden permanecer en el teléfono incluso después de desinstalar el programa que los creó o permitió gestionarlos.
Una fotografía editada con una aplicación, por ejemplo, puede continuar disponible en la galería del celular. Por eso, antes de eliminar herramientas de edición de imágenes, grabación de audio, gestión de documentos u otras aplicaciones que trabajen con archivos personales, conviene revisar qué contenido queda almacenado en el dispositivo.
PUBLICIDAD
Desinstalar no elimina tu cuenta
Este es uno de los errores más habituales. Si un usuario elimina Instagram, Spotify, Netflix, WhatsApp u otra aplicación vinculada a una cuenta, no necesariamente está eliminando su perfil.
La cuenta y buena parte de su información pueden permanecer almacenadas en los servidores de la compañía. Esto permite que una persona vuelva a instalar la aplicación meses después, inicie sesión y recupere su información.
PUBLICIDAD
Por eso es necesario diferenciar tres elementos: la aplicación instalada, los datos almacenados localmente y los datos asociados a la cuenta. Eliminar el primero no implica necesariamente eliminar los otros dos.
Las copias de seguridad también importan
Otro factor que puede conservar información son las copias de seguridad. Android y iOS permiten respaldar determinados datos del dispositivo y, dependiendo de la aplicación y de su configuración, algunos de ellos pueden formar parte de esas copias.
PUBLICIDAD
Esto puede provocar que determinada información reaparezca cuando se reinstala una aplicación o cuando se restaura un teléfono desde una copia anterior.
Además, muchos servicios cuentan con almacenamiento en la nube. En estos casos, el contenido no se encuentra físicamente en el celular, sino en servidores externos. La aplicación simplemente permite acceder a esos datos.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo borrar realmente tus datos
Si la intención es dejar de utilizar un servicio y evitar que conserve información personal, desinstalar la aplicación no es suficiente.
Lo primero es buscar dentro de la propia plataforma una opción para eliminar la cuenta. Normalmente se encuentra en los apartados de configuración, privacidad o gestión de la cuenta. El procedimiento cambia según cada servicio y, en algunos casos, la eliminación puede requerir pasos adicionales.
PUBLICIDAD
También es importante revisar las suscripciones. Borrar una aplicación no cancela automáticamente un pago recurrente. Si existe una suscripción contratada mediante Google Play, App Store o directamente con el proveedor, debe cancelarse desde el sistema correspondiente.
En definitiva, desinstalar una aplicación sirve principalmente para retirar el programa del teléfono y liberar espacio. No debe confundirse con borrar una cuenta ni con eliminar todos los datos asociados al servicio. Si la privacidad es la prioridad, es necesario revisar por separado los archivos locales, las copias de seguridad, la información almacenada en la nube y las opciones de eliminación de la cuenta.

articles.title: 5 ways ChatGPT can become your secret weapon for the new school year
articles.text:
Before you go back to school, set up these 5 ChatGPT tools — your future self will thank you
The latest learning tools can organize your semester and help you study
ChatGPT has accumulated a surprisingly large collection of education tools, including Study Mode and new plugins designed specifically for college students and educators.
The trick is using them to learn rather than outsourcing the learning itself. OpenAI explicitly describes its approach as helping students understand material rather than simply shortcutting it, which is a useful rule to keep in mind before handing ChatGPT the first assignment of the semester.
Here are five ways I would set up ChatGPT before classes get properly underway.
1. Study Mode for all
ChatGPT's aptly named Study Mode is the obvious place to start with using the AI for learning, and it doesn't even require a paid subscription. You simply start a normal conversation with ChatGPT and type @study, or click the + button and search for Study.
Once activated, Study Mode changes ChatGPT's responses from direct answers to more Socratic behavior. It asks questions, provides hints, and checks whether you understand each step before moving forward.
Try prompts like, "Teach me derivatives, asking one question at a time, and give me a hint when I'm stuck."
You can also upload a photo of a problem or, where file uploads are available, add your class notes and ask ChatGPT to work from those. For instance, you could upload what you wrote down in class and tell ChatGPT to "Use these notes to teach me today's lesson. Start by identifying and explaining concepts I need to understand, then quiz me before moving to the next."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Study Mode can work with uploaded files and images, making it much more useful when it knows what your actual class is covering rather than delivering a generic miniature lecture.
2. ChatGPT College Plugin
A newer and more focused option is ChatGPT's College Student plugin. It's not universally available like Study Mode, only through ChatGPT Edu, so your university needs to offer it and make it available. Students who can access it get a collection of learning tools.
Of particular interest is its interactive learning site creation. You can share your course material to make interactive visual explanations, while also getting guided tutoring on concepts you find difficult. The AI can take uploaded lecture slides or notes and make a unique website full of study questions and able to provide feedback on your answers.
Depending on how confident you feel, you could ask ChatGPT for something as elaborate as, "Build me a study plan for the next two weeks using these course materials and my upcoming deadlines, and spend extra time on the topics I struggled with in the quiz."
3. Syllabus study
My memory of student life is that the syllabus traditionally enjoys about 20 minutes of intense attention before beginning its long journey toward the bottom of a backpack. ChatGPT can make it considerably more useful. Upload the syllabus to ChatGPT, and it can have a much more productive lifespan.
I'd suggest a prompt like, "Read this syllabus and create a week-by-week study plan. Include every test, paper, and deadline. Suggest what I should begin preparing for at least a week ahead of time."
You can ask about the extra busy weeks and ideas on making them as easy as possible too. If you let ChatGPT send you alerts, you might avoid the end-of-semester crunch when every deadline hits at once and you still only have 24 hours a day to study.
4. Flashcards
ChatGPT can also save you from spending an entire evening making flashcards instead of studying them. You can ask it to make flashcards from your notes, telling it to "Focus on particulalry confusing concepts and terms."
If you ask for one card at a time, it turns the exercise into an actual study session instead of generating another giant page of material to stare at, hopefully.
With the College Student plugin, flashcards can become part of the interactive learning experience rather than simply appearing as text in the conversation. You could ask: "Turn this week's lecture material into flashcards and organize them by topic."
5. Quiz time
Quizzing you on whether you actually have learned anything from studying is vital, and ChatGPT can be a big help in that regard. With its Study Mode, you can create practice questions, quiz yourself one question at a time, get it to explain mistakes and change the difficulty as you progress.
Upload your course material and try asking for a "10-question practice quiz based only on these notes. Ask one question at a time, don't reveal the answer until I respond, explain anything I get wrong, and make the next question harder when I answer correctly."
The College Student plugin can turn that same process into a more structured interactive quiz built around the course sources you provide. You can ask for more complex practice exams, and set up interactive tests that analyze your weakest areas for further study and quizzing.
With or without the plug-in, having ChatGPT close the metaphorical book and start asking questions is a much faster way to discover whether anything actually stuck.

articles.title: Looking to ditch Kindle? Here are the alternative ereaders we rate most highly
articles.text:
The best Kindle alternatives — excellent ereaders for anyone who's had enough of Amazon's antics
Want to ditch Kindle? These are the ereaders we'd recommend
Once upon a time, if you wanted a good ereader, you simply had to buy a Kindle. When it came to electronic reading devices, Amazon's Kindle lineup ruled the roost. Nowadays, the market has opened up, and Amazon has made a few moves that have done nothing to boost the general public's opinion of Kindles.
The latest Kindle update sparking complaints is the introduction of tougher DRM (digital rights management) rules and the closing of a book-borrowing loophole. Now, we're not sure this particular outrage is particularly justified — as TechRadar's Lance points out, "writers gotta get paid", and authors' ability to make money off their work should take priority, whatever annoyances it might throw up for individual readers.
Less easy to justify, however, is Amazon's April decision to end support for Kindles made in 2012 or earlier. That meant these perfectly usable devices would lose access to the Kindle Store and become completely defunct if you ever tried a factory reset. Overall, Kindles are starting to look a little less enticing to many people.
If you've decided it's time to embrace a different ereader brand, there are a number of great options open to you nowadays, with models from Kobo leading the charge, and Onyx Boox also coming up with some intriguing alternatives. I've rounded up our top-rated Kindle alternatives below — hit the 'More details' button to see the main pros and cons of each, and for a link to our full review.
Kindle alternatives
What's the best Kindle alternative?
The key rival nipping at Amazon's heels is Kobo. The Kobo Libra Colour is the best ereader we've tested, from any brand (including Amazon Kindle), and we also rate the Kobo Clara Colour highly. For those happy to stick with black and white, and looking for a budget-friendly option, the Kobo Clara BW is a winner.
Outside of Kobo, the Onyx Boox lineup is also worth checking out. Its e-ink tablets run on an Android OS, making them nice and versatile. The Boox Palma 2 and Palma 2 Pro are phone-sized ereaders that can be slipped into a pocket for reading on the go.
If you'd like an ereader that also supports note-taking, there are a few more brands worth considering. We're huge fans of the reMarkable Paper Pure, and we also rate the ViWoods AiPaper highly. I'm assuming reading is your main priority, so I haven't included these options here.

articles.title: Papelera de WhatsApp: por qué limpiarla ayuda a mejorar el rendimiento del celular
articles.text:
Limpiar la “papelera” de WhatsApp ayuda a mejorar el rendimiento del celular porque elimina archivos que el usuario cree borrados, pero que todavía siguen ocupando espacio en la memoria del dispositivo.
Esa liberación no solo reduce las alertas de almacenamiento lleno: también evita que se acumulen fotos, videos y documentos innecesarios que terminan afectando el funcionamiento general del teléfono y de la propia aplicación.
PUBLICIDAD
En la práctica, cuando se habla de “papelera” en WhatsApp se hace referencia a una opción dentro de la administración de almacenamiento que permite gestionar y borrar definitivamente archivos eliminados de los chats, pero que aún permanecen guardados en el teléfono.
Es decir: funciona como un espacio intermedio desde el cual se puede revisar lo que quedó almacenado y decidir qué se elimina de manera permanente (y, en algunos casos, recuperar contenido borrado por error antes de su eliminación definitiva).
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo limpiar la papelera de WhatsApp
Para acceder a esta sección, WhatsApp dispone de un recorrido específico dentro de la app. El usuario debe ingresar a Ajustes, luego ir a Almacenamiento y datos y, finalmente, entrar en Administración de almacenamiento.
Dentro de ese apartado, debajo de la sección destinada a revisar y eliminar elementos, aparece la opción de seleccionar archivos y borrar definitivamente aquellos que ya no se desean conservar.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta limpieza puede hacerse de forma periódica para evitar que se acumulen archivos innecesarios, mantener el dispositivo más liviano y prevenir problemas vinculados con el almacenamiento lleno.
Qué otras funciones de WhatsApp ayudan a optimizar el almacenamiento
Más allá del uso de esta “papelera”, WhatsApp ofrece otras alternativas para reducir el consumo de memoria. Una de las principales recomendaciones es revisar los chats de grupos, ya que suelen ser los que más contenido multimedia generan.
PUBLICIDAD
En esos grupos, eliminar fotos, videos, GIF, stickers y documentos innecesarios puede hacer una diferencia notable en el espacio disponible.
También es útil modificar la configuración de descarga automática: desde los ajustes de la app, se puede desactivar la descarga para ciertos tipos de archivos —como videos o documentos— y evitar que se acumulen sin que el usuario lo advierta.
PUBLICIDAD
Otra medida relevante es controlar los respaldos automáticos. Las copias de seguridad de conversaciones pueden incluir archivos multimedia y ocupar espacio tanto en el teléfono como en servicios en la nube.
Revisar la configuración y limitar el alcance de esos respaldos ayuda a prevenir un crecimiento desmedido del almacenamiento consumido.
Si el problema de espacio es más general, conviene realizar una limpieza más amplia del teléfono: eliminar aplicaciones que no se usan, borrar contenido duplicado en la galería y trasladar fotos y videos a servicios de almacenamiento en la nube como Google Fotos o iCloud.
PUBLICIDAD
Vaciar la caché de las aplicaciones también puede resultar efectivo, ya que con el uso se acumulan datos temporales que, según el caso, llegan a ocupar varios gigabytes.
Qué nuevas funciones hay en WhatsApp
En los últimos meses, WhatsApp incorporó funciones para mejorar la organización de los chats y la comodidad de uso en distintos dispositivos.
Entre esas novedades se incluye la posibilidad de registrar una cuenta directamente desde iPad, sin depender de un teléfono vinculado.
La integración con sistemas de automóviles también se optimizó: ahora la aplicación es compatible con Apple CarPlay y Android Auto, lo que permite escuchar y responder mensajes, realizar llamadas, revisar el historial y acceder a favoritos desde la pantalla del vehículo, con manos libres.
PUBLICIDAD
En lo que respecta a los grupos, WhatsApp amplió herramientas para tomar decisiones de forma colaborativa. Las encuestas incorporaron opciones como fijar un horario de cierre, ocultar los nombres de quienes votan y editar la pregunta durante los primeros 15 minutos tras su publicación.

articles.title: Claude wins out in major user satisfaction survey, beating Gemini and ChatGPT — but it's bad news for Grok and Siri
articles.text:
Claude wins out in major user satisfaction survey, beating Gemini and ChatGPT — but it's bad news for Grok and Siri
Claude satisfies the parts other AIs cannot reach
- Claude AI has the highest satisfaction score among current and former users with a net score of 56.2, ahead of Gemini at 46.5
- Grok and Siri languish at the bottom of the satisfaction ratings top 10
- The data was collected by YouGov in the period March 1, 2026 to July 31, 2026
A new YouGov survey has lifted the lid on how people feel about the AI tools and assistants they use, with Claude AI coming out on top with the highest satisfaction score. Anthropic’s AI has beaten OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google Gemini into first place, but of interest are the tools that languish at the bottom of the table.
While Microsoft Copilot and Alexa hog the middle of the table, it is the reputation of Apple’s Siri assistant and Elon Musk’s Grok that are the most surprising, with respondents reporting that the tools did not satisfy.
Interestingly, Claude is also highly regarded among former users, which may indicate that competing tools (particularly those with a poorer reputation) have a lot of catching up to do in the public consciousness.
Everyone loves Claude
Collected over a five-month period, YouGov established two sets of data: the “Top 10 AI assistants by Satisfaction among current and former users” and “AI assistant Satisfaction: current vs. former users.”
Based on the “Top 10 AI assistants by Satisfaction among current and former users” Claude’s 56.2 score puts it markedly ahead of Gemini on 46.5, with ChatGPT a close third on 46.0. Grok and Siri are notable for their low positions, but Alexa (42.6) and Copilot (37.2) occupy a middle space that doesn’t quite seem to match with the size of the companies behind them.
However, one thing that the survey doesn’t tell us is how the Satisfaction metric might be affected by tools that are easy to find or use (for example, Siri or Alexa) versus AI tools that need to be sought out, such as ChatGPT or Claude.
AI tool reputations
YouGov’s data also explores the difference between the satisfaction of current users and former users in the “AI assistant Satisfaction: current vs. former users” results. This again supports the notion that Claude delivers more usable results, with it gaining the highest “Former users Satisfaction score” as well as the second highest “Current users Satisfaction score.”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The report states “The widest current-versus-former gaps appear for ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Grok. ChatGPT is 63.7 points higher among current users than former users; DeepSeek is 62.5 points higher, and Grok is 62.4 points higher.” Grok has a particularly low score among former users: -4.7!
The data was collected by YouGov’s BrandIndex tracking system, a tool that interrogates the live users on YouGov with targeted questions about specific topics or news stories. To learn about AI tool reputation, YouGov collected data over a five month period, between March 1, 2026 and July 31, 2026, focusing on users in the UK.

Christian Cawley has extensive experience as a writer and editor in consumer electronics, IT and entertainment media. He has contributed to TechRadar since 2017 and has been published in Computer Weekly, Linux Format, ComputerActive, and other publications.
He currently heads up the team at smart home website Matter Alpha, and writes about retro gaming at Gaming Retro.

articles.title: Xbox Series X25: una filtración adelanta cuánto costaría la nueva consola de Microsoft
articles.text:
La Xbox Series X25, edición especial con la que Microsoft conmemorará los 25 años de Xbox, podría llegar al mercado el próximo 27 de noviembre, coincidiendo con el Black Friday. Además, una filtración apunta a que la consola tendría un precio de 899 dólares en Estados Unidos.
La información procede del conocido filtrador billbil-kun, quien asegura haber encontrado datos sobre el precio y la fecha de lanzamiento del dispositivo. Microsoft confirmó oficialmente la existencia de esta edición limitada durante el Xbox Games Showcase de junio, pero todavía no ha anunciado cuánto costará ni cuándo comenzarán las ventas.
PUBLICIDAD
Si la información termina siendo correcta, la Xbox Series X25 será considerablemente más cara que la Xbox Series X convencional. El precio filtrado la situaría además en un nivel similar al de la PlayStation 5 Pro, por lo que Microsoft estaría dirigiendo este modelo especialmente a coleccionistas y seguidores de la marca.
Una Xbox Series X pensada para coleccionistas
La Xbox Series X25 recuperará elementos visuales relacionados con la primera consola de Microsoft, lanzada en Estados Unidos el 15 de noviembre de 2001.
PUBLICIDAD
En lugar del tradicional acabado negro de la Series X, esta edición limitada utilizará una carcasa verde semitransparente que permitirá apreciar parte de los elementos internos de la consola. También contará con grabados y detalles especiales relacionados con el aniversario de Xbox.
Entre los elementos distintivos estará el botón de encendido, que utilizará iluminación verde, además de un logotipo conmemorativo situado en la parte frontal. Microsoft también ha incluido pequeños guiños destinados a los seguidores de la compañía y de la historia de Xbox.
PUBLICIDAD
El diseño busca recuperar la estética de los productos tecnológicos de comienzos de los años 2000, cuando las carcasas transparentes y translúcidas se convirtieron en una de las tendencias más reconocibles de la industria.
El mando también tendrá un diseño especial
La consola llegará acompañada de un Xbox Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition, diseñado para combinar con el aspecto de la Xbox Series X25.
El mando utilizará igualmente una carcasa translúcida y contará con elementos inspirados en el controlador original de Xbox, conocido popularmente como Duke. Entre ellos destacan los colores originales de los botones ABXY y diferentes detalles relacionados con los primeros años de la marca.
PUBLICIDAD
Microsoft también ha confirmado que este mando podrá adquirirse por separado, aunque todavía no se conoce el precio de venta individual.
No habrá mejoras en el hardware
A pesar de su precio, la Xbox Series X25 no incorporará un salto de rendimiento respecto al modelo convencional.
En su interior seguirá utilizando la configuración de la Xbox Series X de 1 TB, por lo que las principales diferencias estarán en el diseño exterior, los accesorios incluidos y su condición de edición limitada.
PUBLICIDAD
Esto significa que los compradores no estarán pagando por una consola más potente, sino por un producto de colección dirigido especialmente a quienes quieran celebrar los 25 años de Xbox.
Llegaría justo para el Black Friday
La fecha filtrada, el 27 de noviembre, situaría el lanzamiento de la Xbox Series X25 en pleno Black Friday. También sería aproximadamente dos semanas después del 25.º aniversario de la primera Xbox.
PUBLICIDAD
La consola original debutó en Estados Unidos el 15 de noviembre de 2001, por lo que Microsoft habría elegido una fecha comercialmente relevante para poner a la venta esta edición especial.
El lanzamiento también se produciría pocos días después de la llegada prevista de Grand Theft Auto VI, cuyo estreno está fijado para el 19 de noviembre. Esto podría convertir noviembre en uno de los periodos de mayor actividad para los jugadores de Xbox.
PUBLICIDAD
Por ahora, Microsoft no ha confirmado oficialmente ni el precio de 899 dólares ni la fecha del 27 de noviembre. Tampoco se conoce cuándo comenzarán las reservas. Por tanto, ambos datos deben considerarse una filtración hasta que la compañía anuncie formalmente las condiciones de lanzamiento.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: After one month with the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, I’m convinced that its passport form factor is the way forward for foldable phones
articles.text:
I’ve spent a month with the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, and this video-friendly phone has turned me into a foldable believer
Just when it looked like foldable phones might fade into irrelevance (they represented just 1.5% of global smartphone sales in 2025), Samsung has come along with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 — a passport-shaped foldable that could, with Apple’s help, catapult dual-screen devices into the mainstream.
We’ve actually seen this form factor before — the Huawei Pura X Max, for instance, debuted in China earlier this year — but the Galaxy Z Fold 8 marks the first time a passport-style foldable has been made available in Western markets.
So, is it as revolutionary as Samsung wants us to believe? I’ve been using the Galaxy Z Fold 8 for exactly a month now, and I can safely say that, yes, it’s a supremely versatile content-watching machine — though there are some quirks to be aware of if you’re thinking of spending $1,899 /£1,699 / AU$2,699 on one.
In this article, I’ll run through what I love, don’t love, and just generally think about Samsung’s new kid on the block. You can also check out our full Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 review for an in-depth look at specific features, or watch the video below for an on-camera rundown of everything I’m about to say.
Calling all video lovers
Let’s kick off with my thoughts on the Z Fold 8’s design, which ditches the productivity-focused dimensions of previous book-style foldables for a squatter, passport shape when closed and a more practical rectangular shape when opened.
Samsung says these dimension tweaks are a response to changing consumer habits (read: we’re all addicted to scrolling in 2026), and it’s easy to see why the Z Fold 8 is a better phone for browsing social media, watching videos, and reading articles than the larger Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.
For starters, the 5.5-inch, 10:16 cover display is perfect for one-handed use of full-sized apps. You don’t have to stretch your thumb to reach the top of the screen, and it’s also much easier to type on this wider display than on taller, narrower book-style foldables.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The phone’s width might make one-handed typing a bit of a challenge for those with smaller hands, but it’s honestly super nostalgic to type with two hands (which is how we all type for the most part anyway), as it feels a bit like using an old BlackBerry phone without the physical keyboard. Remember those?
Turn the Z Fold 8 on its side, and this cover screen becomes a 16:10 canvas that’s perfectly sized for YouTube videos, Netflix movies, and other video content. The content's aspect ratio stays the same as on any other phone, but in this orientation, the Z Fold 8 removes awkward pillarboxing for a more immersive viewing experience.
I did find that my hand would sometimes cover the bottom-firing speaker when I held the phone like this, but half-unfolding the Z Fold 8 and letting it stand independently has honestly become one of my favorite ways to watch video on any phone.
All this being said, you’re not buying a foldable to use one screen only, and opening up the Z Fold 8 gives you a glorious 7.6-inch, 4:3 display that’s — you guessed it! — also great for video.
On the front display, most video content is cropped by default to 16:9, but you still get smaller black bars here and less negative space than you would on something like the Z Fold 8 Ultra. But the Z Fold 8 really shines when displaying native 4:3 content like older anime shows.
I mean, just *look* at this Neon Genesis Evangelion episode on Netflix and tell me there’s a better way to watch TV on a phone:
And you can say the same for reading. Using the unfolded Z Fold 8 in portrait is great for scrolling through websites, ebooks, and comics because 3:4 isn’t too far off the dimensions of traditional physical books.
This also makes the Z Fold 8 a great size for work-focused apps like Google Docs. While the Z Fold 8 Ultra is definitely more geared towards productivity, I found that the content-focused size of this smaller model isn’t totally unsuitable for professional tasks.
One thing I have noticed, though, is that social media apps aren’t well-optimized for this unfolded screen. 3:4 isn’t too bad for Instagram, but as soon as you switch to landscape, the app just isn’t formatted nicely, so for the most part I’ve been scrolling through socials on the cover display, which feels much more normal by comparison.
And a final word on the phone’s design: the crease here is definitely less visible than it is on the Galaxy Z Fold 7. Samsung added a Flex Titanium layer to both Z Fold 8 models this year, which also makes the hinge feel sturdier, and the phone unfold completely flat. And while phones like the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Honor Magic V6 offer better dust resistance, I’ve never worried about the durability of my Z Fold 8.
Pocketable power
In terms of performance, the Z Fold 8 is just as fun to use as it is to look at. It’s got a top-of-the-line Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset and 12GB of RAM, so games like Asphalt Legends run smoothly at their highest graphical settings.
Samsung has also updated its Multi-Window feature so you can use up to three apps side-by-side vertically or horizontally, as well as via the older splitting method. I can’t say I’ve ever needed to use three apps simultaneously, but having two apps open side-by-side is definitely useful for cross-referencing info while working, and if you’re really unhinged, you can scroll through Reels AND TikTok at the same time.
Now Nudge has been updated too, and will open suggested apps in split-screen, which is a nice way to encourage you to use the full potential of the foldable phone you've just spent so much money on.
Camera compromises
Right, enough of the good stuff — let’s talk about what you lose by choosing this type of foldable over another.
The biggest compromise comes in the camera department, as while the Z Fold 8’s main and ultra-wide snappers are decent enough, there’s no form of telephoto camera to speak of here, which is… pretty wild considering how much this phone costs.
The 50MP main camera does offer 2x in-sensor zoom for a little extra reach when you need it, but you’ll start to lose image quality when zooming digitally up to 10x. Thankfully, the main and ultra-wide cameras you do get are pretty solid, offering vibrant colors and plenty of detail, but you will get sharper images on the more camera-focused Z Fold 8 Ultra.
Here's a picture-by-picture comparison of the two phones' photography capabilities, as captured by TechRadar contributor Tom Bedford:
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
That said, selfies are great, and portrait mode is still a Samsung strength, while Smart video features like Super Steady video with Horizontal Lock and My FanCam keep the Z Fold 8 feeling fun and fresh. The former levels out shaky footage at the expense of some resolution, while the latter lets you create a motion-tracked video of a particular subject from any video.
My FanCam is pretty effective, though, as we explained in our review of the phone; the subject needs to be well lit and large enough in the frame for Samsung’s algorithm to identify. There’s no manual tracking option, so you’re at the mercy of the feature as to whether your footage is compatible.
Battery life is another good-but-not-great aspect of the Galaxy Z Fold 8. Yes, it’s the first Samsung phone to feature a silicon-carbon battery, and yes, it has better battery life than the Z Fold 7 — but you won’t get Honor- or Oppo-level endurance here.
Samsung says you’ll get 26 hours of video playback from a single charge of the Z Fold 8, and that’s true, but only if you stick to the cover screen. In reality, a day with the phone means switching between screens, watching YouTube videos in unfolded mode, maybe gaming a bit — and as such, the real battery life figure lands closer to somewhere between a day and a day-and-a-half.
Mind you, that’s still… pretty good! I charge my phone every night anyway, so I haven’t been left in the lurch with a dead Z Fold 8, but I don’t think the inclusion of silicon-carbon technology here is the revolution that some people (including me) maybe hoped it would be.
The Honor Magic V6, for context, uses a larger 6,600mAh battery that lasts for well over two days, and that’s a figure that not even the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra can touch.
For charging, you’re getting 45W wired speeds, which will get you to 50% in around 25 minutes and a full charge in about an hour, and again, those are perfectly good if not exceptional numbers.
You also get 20W wireless charging, but as with every other Samsung phone, you’ll need to buy a magnetic case to make use of it, as the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have any built-in magnets.
One month verdict
Overall, I’ve really enjoyed my time with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 so far, and have been pleasantly surprised by just how well this new form factor works for most things I do on my phone every day.
Videos look great on both displays; I love typing on the cover screen and reading on the inner screen, and the Z Fold 8 is also powerful enough to be a nice little gaming machine.
You’ll get better cameras and battery life by choosing a regular flagship phone or the more expensive Z Fold 8 Ultra, but none of those devices will feel as fun or special as the Z Fold 8.
To be honest, I feel similarly about this phone as I do the iPhone Air. It seems weird and silly at first — and you’re paying a lot of money for fewer flagship features — but the Z Fold 8 is just very fun to use day-to-day, and it brings back some of the excitement that foldable phones have been missing.
If the rumors are true and Apple is indeed releasing a similarly sized iPhone Ultra later this year, this new form factor has a real chance of taking off — but as things stand right now, the Z Fold 8 is the foldable to buy if, like me, consuming content is what you do best.
