Sous le capot, l'appareil disposerait, selon les rumeurs, d’un processeur Kirin 9030S, couplé à 12 Go de mémoire vive et jusqu'à 1 To de stockage. Côté photo, un bloc horizontal en forme de pilule abriterait un triple module de 50 mégapixels. Déjà ouvert aux précommandes en Chine sur le site officiel du constructeur, le Pura X View dévoilera l'ensemble de sa fiche technique et ses tarifs officiels le 28 août prochain. articles.title: En 1948 California levantó una ciudad para 4.000 mineros. Hoy es uno de los pueblos fantasma más grandes de EEUU
articles.text:
California necesitó enormes cantidades de hierro para alimentar su expansión industrial de posguerra. Su solución fue tan ambiciosa como el momento: levantar una ciudad entera en mitad del desierto para alojar a los trabajadores que extraerían ese mineral. Durante décadas funcionó como una comunidad autosuficiente. Hoy, sus calles vacías siguen recordando hasta qué punto una industria puede construir (y borrar) una ciudad.
Una ciudad nacida para alimentar la industria del acero. En 1948, el empresario Henry J. Kaiser fundó Eagle Mountain en pleno desierto de California con un único objetivo: explotar uno de los mayores yacimientos de hierro del oeste de Estados Unidos.
No hablamos de un simple campamento minero. Era una ciudad diseñada desde cero para unas 4.000 personas, conectada por un ferrocarril de más de 80 kilómetros con la acería de Fontana, donde el mineral se transformaba en acero.
Una comunidad donde no faltaba absolutamente de nada. La ciudad creció al ritmo de la mina. Llegó a contar con más de 400 viviendas, colegios, iglesias, piscina, bolera, campo de béisbol, centro comercial y un hospital completamente equipado.
Sus calles ajardinadas y sus casas con aire acondicionado simbolizaban el optimismo industrial de la posguerra: si la mina funcionaba, Eagle Mountain tenía todo lo necesario para que varias generaciones hicieran allí su vida.
La mina que también cambió la sanidad estadounidense. La importancia de Eagle Mountain fue mucho más allá del hierro. Kaiser implantó allí un sistema sanitario integrado para atender a los trabajadores y sus familias, con asistencia médica incluida como parte del empleo.
Aquel modelo, ensayado en sus explotaciones industriales, acabaría convirtiéndose en la base de Kaiser Permanente, una de las mayores organizaciones sanitarias de Estados Unidos.
Treinta y cinco años bastaron para vaciar toda una ciudad. El éxito, sin embargo, duró menos de lo esperado. En los años setenta comenzaron a pesar la competencia del acero extranjero, el aumento de los costes ambientales y las dificultades económicas del sector. La producción alcanzó cifras récord en 1975, pero pocos años después llegaron los despidos.
En 1981 se anunció el cierre progresivo de la mina y, en 1983, Eagle Mountain dejó prácticamente de existir: cerraron el supermercado, se graduó la última promoción del instituto y la población abandonó la ciudad casi de un día para otro.
Mientras Estados Unidos cerraba una fábrica, China se la llevaba pieza a pieza. El declive de Eagle Mountain coincidió con otro símbolo del cambio económico mundial. La gigantesca acería de Kaiser en Fontana, considerada una de las más modernas del planeta cuando se inauguró, cerró apenas unos años después.
En 1999, unos 300 trabajadores chinos desmontaron sus 55.000 toneladas de estructuras y maquinaria, las embalaron cuidadosamente y las enviaron por barco para reconstruir toda la instalación en China. Una infraestructura diseñada para durar para siempre terminaba alimentando el auge industrial de otro país.
Un pueblo fantasma congelado en el tiempo. A diferencia de otros asentamientos mineros, Eagle Mountain nunca fue demolido. De hecho, gran parte de sus edificios siguen en pie: las viviendas, el hospital, los comercios e incluso muchas de sus calles permanecen prácticamente intactos bajo el sol del desierto.
Durante un tiempo algunas instalaciones se reutilizaron como prisión, y años después Hollywood encontró allí el escenario perfecto para rodar escenas de la Tenet de Nolan. Mientras tanto, antiguos vecinos siguen reuniéndose para recordar el lugar donde crecieron.
El último misterio de Eagle Mountain. Décadas después de quedar abandonada, la ciudad volvió a captar la atención en los medios cuando un comprador adquirió todo el recinto por 22,5 millones de dólares. Lo cierto es que sus planes nunca se explicaron con claridad y el futuro del lugar continúa siendo una incógnita.
Entre tanto, Eagle Mountain permanece junto al Parque Nacional Joshua Tree como uno de los pueblos fantasma más grandes y mejor conservados de Estados Unidos: una ciudad construida para sostener la industria del acero que hoy sobrevive como una cápsula del tiempo en mitad del desierto.

articles.title: Climatiseur : le Midea PortaSplit est de retour en stock sous les 900€ (avec livraison rapide)
articles.text:
Alors que la canicule n'a pas totalement lâché prise sur la France et que le Midea PortaSplit reste compliqué à dénicher depuis le début de l'été, ce climatiseur split mobile fait son retour chez JoyBuy à 899 euros, sous son tarif conseillé de 999 euros. Nous avons passé en revue cette offre à la lumière de notre test complet, entre performances de refroidissement vérifiées et concessions à connaître avant de craquer.
Lancé au printemps 2026, le Midea PortaSplit s'est rapidement imposé comme une référence chez les locataires en quête de fraîcheur, au point de disparaître des rayons dès le mois de juin. Ce climatiseur associe une unité intérieure montée sur roulettes à une unité extérieure compacte, reliées par une gaine scellée en usine, pour reproduire les performances d'un vrai split fixe sans intervention d'un professionnel. Sa gamme se décline en deux puissances, 8 000 et 12 000 BTU, cette dernière étant seule réversible. JoyBuy propose actuellement la version 12 000 BTU réversible à 899 euros pendant que les stocks le permettent, soit une remise de 100 euros sur le tarif conseillé par Midea.
Une offre qui peut avoir du sens pour les foyers encore à la recherche d'une solution de rafraîchissement avant l'automne, à condition d'accepter les concessions d'un appareil pensé pour rester en place plutôt que pour voyager d'une pièce à l'autre.
Voici le Midea PortaSplit 12 000 BTU à 899 € au lieu de 999 € chez JoyBuy !
Pourquoi choisir le Midea PortaSplit 12 000 BTU ?
- Un vrai split sans installation professionnelle : l'unité extérieure se fixe sur un rebord de fenêtre, un balcon ou une terrasse en quelques minutes, sans perçage ni intervention d'un frigoriste, ce qui convient parfaitement à la location.
- Un prix sous la barre des 900 euros : JoyBuy affiche actuellement l'appareil à 899 euros, quand la plupart des enseignes françaises pratiquent le tarif conseillé de 999 euros, voire davantage en période de forte demande.
- Une note de 8/10 dans notre test complet : notre rédaction a mesuré des performances de refroidissement solides, un confort acoustique correct et une consommation raisonnable, entre 1,40 et 2 euros par 24 heures d'utilisation continue.
Un climatiseur pensé pour les locataires et les petits logements
Le PortaSplit vise en priorité les locataires qui ne peuvent pas installer une climatisation fixe, ainsi que les habitants de logements où les travaux posent problème. Sa version 12 000 BTU annonce une puissance frigorifique de 3,5 kW pour des pièces allant jusqu'à 42 m², avec un mode réversible utilisable comme chauffage d'appoint l'hiver. Dans notre test complet du Midea PortaSplit, la rédaction Clubic a mesuré une baisse de température de 28 à 24-25 degrés en moins de deux heures dans un espace de 70 m², alors qu'il faisait 34 degrés à l'extérieur. L'appareil se pilote via une télécommande, des commandes tactiles, ou l'application Midea SmartHome, compatible avec Google Home et Amazon Alexa.
Face aux climatiseurs monoblocs et aux autres splits mobiles
Comparé à un climatiseur mobile monobloc classique, le PortaSplit évite la dépression d'air qui fait entrer de la chaleur par les interstices d'une fenêtre, pour un confort acoustique nettement supérieur et un meilleur rendement énergétique. Il reste toutefois plus cher et plus lourd que ces modèles, et fait désormais face à des concurrents reprenant le même principe de split mobile, comme le Qlima QsplitFlex ou le Krone Argo Ulisse.
✅ Les points forts
- Des performances de refroidissement confirmées par notre test, y compris dans un logement de 70 m² par forte chaleur
- Un concept split mobile qui allie l'efficacité d'un vrai split à l'absence de travaux
- Une installation qui ne prend qu'une dizaine de minutes, sans perçage ni professionnel
- Un mode réversible utilisable comme chauffage d'appoint pendant l'hiver
- Une consommation électrique raisonnable, entre 1,40 et 2 euros par jour d'utilisation continue
❌ Les limites
- Un appareil semi-mobile de 45,5 kg, peu pratique à déplacer d'une pièce à l'autre ou d'un étage à l'autre
- Une gaine de liaison assez rigide, qui peut limiter certaines configurations d'installation
- Un tarif qui reste élevé malgré la remise, même sous son prix conseillé
- Une disponibilité fluctuante, avec des retours en stock parfois de courte durée chez les revendeurs
Le Midea PortaSplit 12 000 BTU à 899 € chez JoyBuy : vérifier la disponibilité
Le Midea PortaSplit reste un climatiseur split mobile convaincant, comme le confirme la note de 8/10 attribuée dans notre test complet : de bonnes performances de refroidissement, une installation simple et une consommation maîtrisée. À 899 euros chez JoyBuy, il redescend sous son tarif conseillé de 999 euros, dans un contexte où le produit reste difficile à trouver depuis plusieurs semaines chez la plupart des enseignes françaises.
Cette offre s'adresse avant tout aux locataires et aux foyers qui cherchent une alternative sérieuse à un split fixe, sans les contraintes d'une installation permanente ni l'accord d'une copropriété. Ceux qui disposent déjà d'un logement adapté à une climatisation fixe auront sans doute intérêt à se tourner vers des solutions plus légères et moins onéreuses.

articles.title: ABH Healthcare SME IPO to open on Monday
articles.text:
ABH Healthcare SME IPO to open on Monday
The public issue is entirely a fresh issue of up to 34.29 lakh equity shares with a price band fixed at Rs 96-102 per share.
Multi-speciality healthcare provider ABH Healthcare's Rs 34.98 crore initial public offering will open on Monday for subscription.
The initial public offering (IPO) will remain open till August 27, with a tentative listing date on September 1.
The company's shares are proposed to be listed on the NSE SME platform Emerge, according to a statement.
The public issue is entirely a fresh issue of up to 34.29 lakh equity shares with a price band fixed at Rs 96-102 per share.
ABH Healthcare plans to use Rs 17 crore of the net proceeds towards debt repayment in part or in full, Rs 5 crore to fund its working capital requirements, and the remaining balance will be used for inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
"As we enter the next phase of our journey as a listed company, we remain focused on strengthening our clinical capabilities, enhancing patient care and building on the trust that Anil Baghi Hospital has established over the years," Saurabh Baghi, Managing Director at ABH Healthcare Ltd, said.
Incorporated in 2021, ABH Healthcare provides healthcare services under the brand name "Anil Baghi Hospital". It operates a 150-bed multi-speciality hospital offering services across 25 medical specialities.
The hospital is empanelled with 30 private and public health insurance providers and third-party administrators.
Its financial performance has strengthened over the last three years. The consolidated revenue rose from Rs 41.38 crore in FY24 to Rs 52.51 crore in FY26.
The company's profit after tax increased more than threefold to Rs 5.64 crore from Rs 1.66 crore during the same period.
Fedex Securities is the sole book-running lead manager for the IPO.

articles.title: Creality's beginner-friendly Falcon A1C laser engraver won me over instantly
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The entry price of this small laser is reflected in the slightly plastic build quality. However, with a fully enclosed design, it definitely scores a wealth of points over open-frame machines. The work area is small, but the potential of that 10W laser on both paper and 3mm ply highlighted just how effective it is. If you're looking for a small, desktop-sized laser for craft and small projects, this is an incredible bargain.
Pros
- +Price
- +Compact enclosed
- +Beginner-friendly
- +Simple automatic focusing
- +Flexible laser modules
Cons
- -Small working area
- -Camera costs extra
- -Accessories add expense
Why you can trust TechRadar
The Creality Falcon A1C is a compact, fully enclosed desktop laser engraver and a leap forward for affordable laser engraving in a format that's far safer than the open designs I often see at this price.
While it’s more affordable, with the full plastic build, it actually pulls many features from far more expensive machines, including the slightly larger Falcon A1. Designed to sit on your desktop, it measures 336 x 377 x 341 mm, giving it an incredibly compact footprint. Essentially, it's designed to be accessible and usable whenever you need it.
While the design aesthetics might not match that of some rivals' larger machines, the workflow and robust build make it an ideal option for education and small studios where you want to experiment with the technology to create items and even have small production runs.
In this review, I had access to the 10W version, and from unboxing to setup it took no longer than 10 minutes. Activation required a single push of the button on the machine, then a few steps, and it was connected to the mobile app.
On the Mac, it took a few more steps, with the wired connection needed first before you can switch over to Wi-Fi, but in both cases it's one setup, and then you don't have to revisit it later.
When it comes to use, the Falcon Design Space software is once again well laid out, as I saw with the Falcon A1 and Falcon T1, and with a few sample designs I was able to cut directly onto the paper and the basswood supplied.
I was instantly impressed with the results, starting with the basic ruler sample. I laid out five from the outset, and with an 18-minute engraving on the small sheet of 3mm ply, the results were actually incredibly impressive, with little scorching or burning, if any, visible.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
After a month of using the machine on small projects, the engraving quality across a wide range of surfaces was consistently good, with the best results coming from wood and paper.
I also had to connect the A1C to the Bambu Lab air filter because I didn't have the Falcon one to use, but it worked perfectly with no issues. So if you already have an air filter, it should work without the dedicated one from Creality.
During the test, I was purely focused on that 10W laser cutting materials on that 150 x 150mm working area. There is a lower-powered option at 5W if you mainly work with paper, and also a 1.2W IR laser module, giving you even more scope for this one small machine.
What surprises me is the price, and whilst that is slightly reflected in the design and materials used, when it comes to pure functionality, this is a level of machine for its size that you just wouldn't have had a couple of years ago. It’s far better than any of the open-frame designs still available on the market.
One thing I would watch for if you're thinking about buying the A1C: note that there are two versions, and the cheapest doesn't include the camera, and that is a major part of the ease of use for this machine.
It also cannot be upgraded, so I'd really spend that extra money to make sure you get the version with the AI camera, which is the one I’m looking at here. I'd also push and get that 10W laser. It makes a huge difference, especially if you're going to be working with wood.
Even if you start working with paper, card, and acrylic, taking that upgrade is definitely something you're going to want to do in the future.
If you just want to laser small objects, then this is an absolutely superb option at an incredible price and a really good complement to the Creality Falcon range. It will be interesting to see where the company takes laser engraving technology next.
Creality Falcon A1C: Price & availability
To me, price Creality has set is great for a small-build entry-level engraver. But in my opinion, opt for the 10W model with AI camera for maximum future-proofing.
The basic 5W Falcon AIC is $199 from Creality or $299 for the 10W model. In the UK, it's similarly priced at £199 for the 5W version and £289 for the 10W.
However, there is a version with an AI camera attached, which is definitely the model that I would go for.
The 5W Falcon A1C with AI camera is priced at $259 at Creality's store, or $379 for the 10W model. In the UK, it's £249 for the 5W AI camera version and £369 for the 10W.
I'm also seeing the models with the AI camera on sale at Amazon in the US and UK, where you can get the 5W for $259 and the 10W for $379. It's more expensive there for UK readers, with the 5W retailing for £326 and the 10W at £445 at the time of review.
Creality Falcon A1C: Design
Connectivity: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth/BLE, USB
Camera: integrated camera on AI Camera model
Unit size: 336 x 377 x 341mm
Accessories: Optional rotary kit, air purifier, flexible fixture and related engraving accessories. Laser modules supported: 5W diode / 10W diode / 1.2W IR
Engraving area: 150 x 150mm
Maximum processing height: 148mm
Maximum working speed: 15,000mm/min
Focus: Automatic
Safety: Class 1, flame detection, tilt detection and USB safety lock
Weight: 9.7kg Basic / 9.8kg AI Camera model
Software: Falcon Design Space; LightBurn compatibility
Computer support: Windows 10 or later; macOS 11 or later; mobile app also available.
The Creality Falcon A1C is an extremely compact, fully enclosed laser engraver that comes in a variety of different options. In this review, I've been looking at the 10W version, which I highly recommend because it works with the widest range of materials and is a great starting point for any hobbyist, small business, or educational facility.
Alongside the A1C, I would also recommend getting the air filter, which uses a tube connected to the vent hole at the back. In this review, I haven't got Creality's version, so I've adapted it for use with the Bambu Lab air filter, which is used with the Bambu Lab H2D.
What I really like about the A1C's design is that it’s so compact, with a footprint of only 336mm wide and 377mm deep. Essentially, it fits neatly on the workshop workbench.
While the design is fully plastic and you can really feel where Creality has pulled back on the material use to make this as affordable as it is, it's still of decent quality and, with its visor lid ensuring that you stay fully protected from any laser rays, it's also a great option if you're just getting into laser engraving and definitely a big step up from the open-frame designs.
The machine itself, while light at just under 10kg, is well designed and sturdy, so it sits firmly on the work surface and stays put as you lift and close the lid. It's also worth highlighting that there is a security USB key on the back, so if you are using this at home and don't want the kids to get close to it, or if you have other people in the office, you can remove the key for safety; without it, the machine isn't usable.
Also, on the safety features, it has all the usual knock and tilt kill switches, as well as lid-lifting alerts. It also has a large safety stop button on the side, so if you are using this in education, it essentially has everything needed to pass most safety checks. However, you will need to check with your institution to make sure it is fully in line.
Now, whilst the build is fully plastic, it's all of really decent quality, and that weight helps ensure minimal vibration from the laser as it works away inside. It also has full autofocus, although you do need to activate it through the app software. It's essentially a pin that lowers with the laser head to touch the material's surface, ensuring the laser is perfectly focused, and you get the best possible cut, engraving, or score.
The system is simple and effective, and throughout the month of testing, it was completely faultless on the small work area, as long as I always remembered to hit that autofocus button before processing.
Another major feature of the model that I've looked at is the AI camera. Now, this produces a preview of the material on the platform, and I found the exposure was a little dark; sometimes, if using a darker material, you can only just make out where it’s placed in the work area. The front section, in contrast, is always perfectly visible.
One of the big differences between this machine and many others that I've looked at, especially at this size, is that, like some 3D printers, it has a raising platform. So essentially you put your material onto the platform, and it raises depending on the height and type of object and material that it’s made from.
This means that despite it being really small, you can also get a rotary attachment that fits perfectly inside, so you can do mugs and cups.
The platform is manually adjusted with a knob on the side, letting you raise or lower it depending on what you're putting inside, or it moves automatically when using the autofocus.
As this is also a compact laser engraver with an air system, you can secure paper and other objects to the platform, and for wood and acrylic there's also the grill platform you can pop those on top of.
Whilst this still feels, in many ways, like an entry-level laser engraving platform, I'm surprised by the volume of features it includes. They've been taken from professional laser engravers, so whilst this is relatively cheap, especially with all the present offers, it actually offers a very compact professional option at an incredible price.
Creality Falcon A1C: Features
In this test, I've been looking at the Creality Falcon A1C 10W diode laser option, which is good for wood, bamboo, paper, cork, cardboard, leather, glass and fabric. There's also a 5W diode laser option available. This is of lesser power, so any ambitions to cut through materials will have to be reduced.
However, if you just want to score or engrave, then the 5W option is actually a good choice. My personal advice would be to spend that little bit extra and go for the 10W version. That way, you are at least future-proofing yourself.
There's also an optional 1.2W IR module available, which enables even more engraving options. Essentially, the diode lasers let you engrave wood, paper, and soft materials, while the IR laser is designed to engrave and mark metals.
Swapping between the heads is relatively easy and, although I didn't have the IR head to test, the process is very straightforward. A simple securing screw can be undone without tools: drop out the head, pop in the new one, and the system automatically recognises the new head and updates the software, ready for you to get started.
Another feature I really like is full autofocus: you put the material you want to engrave underneath, hit autofocus, the head touches the material, and it focuses the beam. It's a mechanical approach, but it worked incredibly well.
Speed-wise, it can engrave at up to 15,000 mm per minute, which is relatively fast for such a small laser. For most of the test, I reduced this to a more standard 6,000 mm per minute for fill and line engraving, and 450 mm per minute for line cutting. These are the default settings, but after testing above and below, I found the factory defaults were by far the best.
One of the things I really liked on the other Falcon machines is that you use the Falcon Design Space software, which is available for Mac, PC, iOS, and Android. It's really easy to use, well thought out and gives you plenty of options.
If you want to use third-party software such as LightBurn, that's also supported, so if you're working with other laser engravers and want everything under one roof, that is possible.
For connectivity, you can connect via Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or USB. Mobile workflows are really easy: connect through Bluetooth or Wi-Fi, quickly upload, select your settings, and move on.
On the Mac/PC, using Falcon Design Space, you initially connect through USB and, once set up, you can connect through Wi-Fi, which gives you plenty of options and has proven to be a really solid way of working.
Alongside the machine, there’s a range of accessories, including the rotary engraver, which is a standard accessory for most engravers. It's great to see it here as an upgrade option. There's also the air purification accessory, which I would definitely recommend if you are thinking of buying this or, for that matter, any laser engraver.
Creality Falcon A1C: Performance
Getting started with a Falcon A1C doesn't take long. It's a small machine, so unboxing and setting it up on the desktop takes no more than five minutes. Once the packaging is removed, the power is plugged in, and the cutting surface is installed, you can lower the platform using the dial on the right-hand side of the machine so the cutting platform and material can be slipped into place.
Before I got started, I also just wanted to check the emergency stop: testing this simply involved hitting the red button. Everything shut down, and it was the usual twist to power the machine back on.
Having a stop button on the side of machines is essential. This button enables you to kill the power, so that if one of the materials that you've popped inside catches fire, you can deal with it quickly. Hit stop, and that kills the power, so you're only dealing with the fire and not the laser moving as well.
I then popped in the first piece of 3mm ply, loaded up the iOS app and quickly ran through a couple of test engraves. I was surprised by how easy it was to connect to the app and get started; it took no more than five minutes.
I then moved over to the MacBook Pro and, again, it took a couple of minutes to connect the USB cable, do a quick test card and then disconnect the Mac, at which point I could use it over Wi-Fi back in the house.
Popping in materials was all easy enough, with that dial on the side basically activating the motor so the platform raises or lowers. You can then place your material in, hit autofocus once the lid is down, and it's then primed and ready to go. Back in the Falcon software, you can activate the camera to preview the material and the design you've loaded, move it around, and you're almost ready to go.
If you've downloaded a pre-designed cutting path from the Creality site, it's very easy, as the different cuts and engraves have already been highlighted. However, if you're importing paths from your chosen software, then you'll need to select the path and allocate line cutting or engraving.
Essentially, if you import your logo and want it to be a placemat with the logo engraved, Then you want the placemat to be cut out in a disc obviously, what you need to do is select the logo as your first engraving layer and assign that as a line engrave, and set the speed to 6,000mm a minute at about 60% with a one-time pass for 3mm basswood board.
Then, for the letters, create another layer with the text, select Fill Engraving, set the speed to 6,000 mm/min and power to 60%, and run one pass. Finally, you want your logo cut out of that mat, so select a circle from the shapes, draw it around your logo, select line cutting, set the speed to 450 m/minute and power to 80% with one pass, go to Processing and wait for your placemat to be cut.
Another level of ease is that there are loads of materials present; just select the material type and a preset for that is loaded. Through this test, I used basswood ply or paper for the majority of cuts, and these materials could be selected in the presets. With the AI camera enabling you to line everything up perfectly, it was very quick and straightforward to start getting impressive results from the outset.
During the test, I found that the small 150 x 150mm work surface was a little restrictive. For example, a placemat for a mug measuring 90mm x 90mm means you can only do one at a time. Also, if you want to do anything larger, then you will need a larger machine. However, for small home projects, there’s still plenty of scope.
The camera, while useful, is also limited. Seeing the material at the top left in the preview can be difficult because of its position on the laser head and, unless you have bright lighting in the workshop, the preview can look a little dark. There’s also a stop on using the camera while the laser is in action; this is just to review the material, not to monitor the project's progress.
Checking the quality of some engraving, it's exceptionally high, with a good, accurate laser delivering outstanding results considering the size and scale of this machine.
For fine detail, as you'll see on some of the coasters, you have to be very careful about how you convert the image for laser engraving. Still, after a few runs and a little bit of experimentation, you'll settle on the best results for the material that you're using.
Likewise, when it comes to cutting, there's very little, if any, scorching, which means that if you are doing small production runs, you can quickly wipe the wood afterwards and go straight to finishing with a bit of wax, depending on what you're doing.
Overall, the performance and quality this small machine can produce are exceptionally high, and for anyone or a small business looking to get into laser engraving, this is a great starting point and will absolutely show what can be done with this technology.
Creality Falcon A1C: Final verdict
Creality Falcon A1C is an interesting machine. It’s a Class 1 laser, and interchangeable modules enable you to swap between a 5W (optional) or 10W diode laser and a 1.2W IR head (Optional), and there's plenty of flexibility in what you can do with this machine.
My one thing to point out is that there are two versions of the machine. Just make sure you're opting for the slightly more expensive one with the AI camera, which is the version I've looked at in this review. The cheaper version doesn't feature the AI camera, so positioning is a little bit trickier, and you can't preview exactly where things go.
When it comes to use, the studio software makes things easy. Although there’s still a learning process, especially with putting your cutting and engraving paths onto different layers, after a few runs it's relatively easy to work out.
If you are totally new, I highly recommend downloading some pre-made templates and seeing how they are made; it all starts to make sense pretty quickly as you click through those layers.
Whilst the machine itself is cheap, you will have to pay extra if you want to purchase many of the accessories, including the 5W diode or IR heads, but even then they're not usually expensive compared with other laser engravers. One real limitation is the 150 x 150 work area, a size I normally associate with a fibre laser, not a diode like this.
However, that small size also means you can easily sit it on a desktop. It's great for a small workshop or anyone wanting to dabble in laser engraving, as it gives you a superb idea of what larger, more expensive machines can do, and 10W in a small machine like this is still substantial enough to create some pretty impressive products.
When it comes to cutting quality, it’s exceptionally good, and the engraving quality is, too; at this level it's well above what you would normally expect.
If you are looking for a small, compact laser engraver, this is a great place to start. I would suggest spending that little extra and buying the air filter at the same time, and if you can afford it, the rotary addition is always a worthwhile accessory.
Should you buy the Creality Falcon A1C
| Value: | Excellent functions and features for a machine at this price, giving you a true taste of what laser engraving is all about | 4.5 | 
| Design: | The full-plastic design has a slightly cheapish feel, but with the small footprint it fits neatly on almost any work surface | 4.5 | 
| Features | The autofocus feature just makes using this laser engraver exceptionally easy, as does the fact that it's fully enclosed, perfect for beginners | 4.5 | 
| Performance | A 150 x 150 work area is slightly limiting, but aside from that, if you just want to work on small items, the cutting and engraving quality is superb | 4.5 | 
| Total | An extremely well-priced and feature-packed compact laser engraver for both beginners and small businesses | 4.5 | 
Buy it if...
It's your first laser engraver
If you want your first fully enclosed laser engraver but don't like the idea of an open machine, this is a superb option at this price and surprisingly feature-packed.
You work on small, personalized products
If you focus on gifts, tags, jewellery, and other small products, the 150 x 150mm work area is a huge benefit and very easy to use.
Don't buy it if...
You need a large work area
If you're making products or multiple parts, the 150 x 150 work area will be a bit small, and if you want to mass-produce, you'll definitely need something bigger.
You may need a camera later
Don't go for the cheaper model without the camera. Whilst it will save you quite a bit of money, it also makes the machine more complicated to use.
For more crafting tech, I've tested and reviewed all the best 3D printers and best laser engravers.
Alastair is a photographer, filmmaker and tech writer who has been working in the publishing industry since the late 1990s. For more than 25 years he has covered photography, video and technology across Future's photography, technology and gaming brands. He runs a photography and video production company and lectures in TV and film. He can usually be found testing mini PCs or prototyping and prop building with the aid of 3D printing.

articles.title: Pensábamos que el mejor ejercicio a los 60 años era caminar. La ciencia apunta a la piscina como el "blindaje" definitivo
articles.text:
Cuando comenzamos a hacernos mayores, hay una recomendación que comienza a generar mucho protagonismo, que es la necesidad de mantenerse activo. Sin embargo, el desgaste articular, el miedo a las caídas o la pérdida de masa muscular suelen complicar la elección del deporte ideal. Y es aquí donde la piscina emerge no como una alternativa más, sino como el entorno biomecánico perfecto.
Cada vez más importancia. Durante los últimos años, la ciencia ha dedicado un buen espacio para analizar los efectos que tiene la natación en nuestro organismo. Y el veredicto es que nadar o hacer gimnasia en el agua a partir de los 60 años produce una transformación integral que abarca desde la musculatura hasta el cerebro.
Es un blindaje. Cuando nos sumergimos en el agua, la flotabilidad reduce drásticamente el impacto en las articulaciones, lo que convierte a la piscina en un santuario para personas con artritis o limitaciones musculoesqueléticas. Pero que el agua sea amable no significa que no sea exigente.
En este caso, un análisis publicado en 2026 analizó a más de 1.100 adultos mayores y demostró que el ejercicio acuático mejora de forma integral la función física. Además, la resistencia natural del agua actúa como una máquina de pesas fluida, logrando aumentos significativos en la fuerza tanto del tren inferior como del superior. Algo que es fundamental para evitar el riesgo de caídas y una ganancia de flexibilidad que es fundamental para cuando nos hacemos mayores.
Corazón de atleta. El impacto que tiene la natación sobre el sistema cardiovascular y metabólico está al nivel de los mejores tratamientos preventivos. Aquí un estudio publicado en 2025 apuntó que el ejercicio acuático combate la rigidez arterial y mejora la función endotelial con una eficacia igual al ejercicio que se puede hacer en un gimnasio en tierra firme.
Y por si fuera poco, la revista Nature publicó recientemente una revisión de 22 estudios que confirma el poder del agua sobre nuestro perfil lipídico. Aquí quedó en evidencia que en la piscina de forma regular reduce el colesterol total, los triglicéridos y el colesterol "malo", mientras eleva el "bueno".
El impacto cerebral. Uno de los descubrimientos más importantes está en los beneficios psicosociales y cognitivos de la natación en los adultos mayores. Aquí la ciencia ha visto que el ejercicio acuático es la modalidad más efectiva para potenciar la función cognitiva, haciendo que se pueda mejorar la memoria, el tiempo de reacción y la atención. Puntos fundamentales cuando se llega a cierta edad.
Además, la interacción social de la hidroginástica y el propio efecto relajante del agua funcionan como un potente antidepresivo y ansiolítico natural, elevando la autoestima y mejorando la calidad de vida general.
La cantidad. Con este pretexto no hace falta ir a un gimnasio a coger mucho peso, sino que yendo 2-3 veces a la semana a una piscina durante unos cuarenta minutos y con una intensidad moderada puede ser más que suficiente. Aquí es donde entra también el hacerlo correctamente, puesto que la receta ideal sería mezclar trabajo de resistencia con ejercicio aeróbico en el agua.

articles.title: Startup success is a Test match, not a T20 game: Accel India co-founder Subrata Mitra on why he backed Flipkart, Myntra, and others
articles.text:
Startup success is a Test match, not a T20 game: Accel India co-founder Subrata Mitra on why he backed Flipkart, Myntra, and others
In this episode of the Prime Venture Partners Podcast, Amit Somani speaks with Accel India co-founder Subrata Mitra to discuss the ideas behind his book Down But Not Out, which brings stories of Indian 10 founders who experienced major setbacks but continued to build.
Subrata Mitra, co-founder at Accel India and an early investor in Flipkart, Myntra, Mu Sigma, and Cult Fit shares what decades of backing Indian startups have taught him about building companies.
There is no such thing as a startup journey that simply goes “up and to the right”.
Subrata Mitra has had one of the best vantage points to make this observation. The co-founder of Accel India, which began as Erasmic Venture Fund, has watched Indian entrepreneurship evolve for over two decades and has backed companies including Flipkart, Myntra and several founders who went through far more complicated journeys before finding success.
“I haven't seen one company that has gone straight up. Up and to the right. Not one. If somebody is telling you that, most likely lying,” says Mitra on the Prime Venture Partners Podcast.
It is also the idea behind Down But Not Out, a book Mitra has co-authored with Pankaj Mishra and other collaborators. Rather than chronicle only celebrated startup successes, the book examines founders who went through failures, pivots and periods when their companies appeared to have run out of road.
For Mitra, those journeys reveal something fundamental about entrepreneurship: the founders who eventually build enduring companies are not necessarily those who avoid setbacks. They are the ones who learn how to remain in the game long enough to capitalise when the right opportunity finally arrives.
Stay at the crease, but know when to hit the six
When Mitra evaluates founders, what does he look for?
“One is this ability to stay long because most journeys in India will go through their own ups and downs,” he says. But endurance alone is insufficient. A founder also needs the judgement to recognise when an opportunity has emerged and the aggression to pursue it.
Mitra explains it through cricket. “You can't defend the entire 50 overs,” he says. “When you get the right ball, you have to also hit the six or the four because the scoreboard also counts.”
The combination matters because startup outcomes can change dramatically from what founders and investors initially imagine. When Accel wrote its first cheque to Flipkart founders Sachin and Binny Bansal, Mitra recalls that a $200-million outcome would have made them happy. The company eventually crossed that milestone without anyone stopping to celebrate it as the destination.
“We went through 200 like that and nobody even looked back and said, you know, that was our milestone. It wasn't. It was just a sort of marker on the road,” he says.
Why Mitra believes in ‘long-term greed’
Mitra has a phrase for this ability to optimise over unusually long periods: “long-term greed”.
The idea comes partly from the nature of venture capital itself. While VC funds may formally have lives of around 10 or 11 years, Mitra says good funds in India can take 14, 15 or even 16 years to fully play out. Accel's 2008-vintage Flipkart fund, he noted, is still alive despite having already returned substantial capital.
“The guys who truly endure are the guys who realise that we are doing it for something else other than greed,” says Mitra.
The book describes entrepreneurship as driving through fog. Founders rarely know exactly what lies ahead, but they still need to keep moving. The “compass”, according to Mitra, is alignment around goals, motivations and people.
“Even though there is fog, you can probably look at the compass and say, I know that I have to do these three things today and that's the north pointer that we are looking at,” he says.
The founder you invest in may have to become someone else
The ability to evolve becomes particularly important because the skills required at one stage of a company can become liabilities at another.
Mitra cites BlueStone founder Gaurav Singh Kushwaha as an example. When Mitra first worked with him, he saw a strong computer scientist and problem solver who was not necessarily equally strong at building and scaling teams. Years later, those responsibilities became unavoidable.
At one difficult point in BlueStone's journey, Kushwaha had to let several employees go. Mitra remembers how he called them into his room individually and began by taking responsibility.“We are doing this, but it is more our fault than your fault,” Kushwaha told them.
Mitra says it can take eight or nine months of working with an early-stage founding team before he develops a meaningful view of whether they have what it takes. Even then, the company itself may fail because of the market or product cycle.
“If you can engage with the right team with the right set of background checks and then keep testing them or keep challenging them for the next six to nine months, they may find something credible or pivot around until they reach innings two, three or four."
Founders must learn to stop doing everything
Evolution also means knowing when to let go. At the beginning, founders are generalists by necessity. Three people may simultaneously handle product, hiring, marketing, research and whatever crisis needs solving that morning.
But that model breaks as the organisation grows. “The big challenge happens when people stop letting go,” says Mitra.
A founder running a 100-person company cannot continue operating as though it has three employees. Instead, Mitra argues that founders need to move their attention from solving every present problem towards anticipating the next stage.
He uses another simple mental model: “What is step 10 going to look like? What is step 100 going to look like?” he says. “When we are at one, we start thinking about 10. When we are at 10, we have to think about 100 and then work backwards from there.”
Complementary founders can make that transition easier. Mitra recalls the early days of Erasmic, when the team was raising a $10 million fund without enough money to hire a lawyer. After Mitra struggled through roughly 20 pages of the private placement memorandum, co-founder Mahendran stepped in to handle it.
“That is the complementarity of skill sets that you need in an initial team that nothing drops to the bottom,” says Mitra.
Coaching should become part of the founder journey
Accel now asks many founders whether they want a coach. The coach could be chosen by the founder or suggested by the firm. Mitra's conviction partly comes from Accel's own experience using coaches and from navigating leadership transitions at companies such as Flipkart.
“I have seen a lot of different variations of coaching work, but it is absolutely essential that most founders get some kind of coaching,” he says.
Mitra describes it as repeatedly coming back to a problem with fresh energy. A success or failure today does not determine what happens tomorrow. “Just because you have either succeeded or failed today, doesn't matter, come back tomorrow, let's take a fresh look and let's just go again. Is it worth going again?”
Make room for joy in a 15-year journey
Endurance, however, cannot mean spending 15 years permanently stressed. Mitra deliberately tries to create an environment at Accel where people can joke about mistakes, including his own. He recalls openly telling colleagues about putting $20 million into a company and questioning his own diligence.
The result, he believes, is not merely a happier workplace. It improves the quality of discussion because people become more comfortable challenging each other.
“Making a little bit of the environment happy, friendly, etc. actually increases the productivity of the system,” he says. When Prime Venture Partners' Amit Somani described entrepreneurship as 363 or 364 days of grind punctuated by one or two days of joy, Mitra offered a different formulation.
“Put that one 365th joy every day.”
Because if entrepreneurship really is a 10 or 15-year journey, waiting for an acquisition, IPO or giant funding round before allowing yourself to enjoy it is an extraordinarily long wait.
Mitra's closing advice to young founders therefore has less to do with markets, fundraising or strategy than with the person running the company.
“You'll probably see a lot of pivots in your ideas, and at the end of it, you have to remain sane and be able to orchestrate that symphony well enough,” he says.
“Work on yourself as to how you get better every day as opposed to thinking of what you can change in the world.”
For a career spent identifying companies capable of changing the world, it is an unexpectedly inward-looking conclusion. But perhaps that is precisely Mitra's point.
Before founders can build something that endures, they have to learn how to endure themselves.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Le prochain PDG d'Apple serait bien plus audacieux et pourrait multiplier les acquisitions
articles.text:
Tim Cook cède la direction générale d’Apple à John Ternus le 1er septembre, après près de quinze ans à ce poste. Bank of America maintient sa recommandation d’achat sur l’action et relève son objectif de cours à 380 dollars, soit environ 325 euros. La banque anticipe une prise de risque accrue sous sa direction, avec de possibles acquisitions.
Le 20 août, l’action Apple était à environ 317 dollars, soit environ 272 euros, en hausse de près de 16 % depuis le début de l’année. Le titre a regagné 4 % lors des deux séances précédentes, sans effacer un retard de 8 % sur son record de juillet. La marque doit présenter sa gamme d’iPhone 18 Pro en septembre, après le succès de l’iPhone 17, dont les ventes ont dépassé de 16 % celles de son prédécesseur lors de son premier trimestre complet. John Ternus, responsable du matériel informatique chez Apple depuis de nombreuses années, prendra la direction générale au moment de ce lancement.
Bank of America table sur un appétit pour le risque plus marqué
L’analyste Wamsi Mohan, de Bank of America, a réitéré sa recommandation d’achat sur Apple et relevé son objectif de cours à 380 dollars, soit environ 325 euros, un potentiel de hausse de près de 20 % par rapport au cours du 20 août. La banque retient, en particulier, l’abandon par Apple de son objectif de trésorerie nette neutre. Bank of America en déduit des dépenses de recherche et développement plus importantes, des investissements en capital accrus et de possibles acquisitions de plus grande envergure, des domaines restés secondaires sous son mandat.
Selon Bank of America, John Ternus pourrait pousser Apple plus vite vers de nouvelles catégories, des lunettes à intelligence artificielle aux bagues connectées, en passant par des AirPods équipés d’une caméra, la domotique, les assistants personnels et la robotique. Connu en interne pour trancher, à la différence de Tim Cook, le futur PDG incarnerait, selon la banque, ce basculement vers davantage d'’audace.
Apple domine le matériel, les puces, les systèmes d’exploitation et l’architecture de confidentialité, avec un parc installé d’un milliard d’appareils, et consoliderait cette avance en associant ces atouts à l’intelligence artificielle embarquée, un basculement du cloud vers des appareils plus autonomes. Sa taille immense est néanmoins son plus grand obstacle. Avec une capitalisation boursière de plus de 4 600 milliards de dollars, soit environ 3 940 milliards d’euros, davantage que le produit intérieur brut annuel de la France, un produit complémentaire réussi compterait moins dans les résultats qu’auparavant. La banque affirme que John Ternus doit préserver ce système rentable, tout en restaurant un esprit de surprise technologique plus marqué.
Quinze ans de records financiers sous Tim Cook
Selon un article de Bloomberg, Apple valait près de 350 milliards de dollars, soit environ 300 milliards d’euros, quand Tim Cook est devenu directeur général en août 2011. Le chiffre d’affaires de l’exercice 2025 a atteint 416,2 milliards de dollars, soit environ 356 milliards d'euros, contre environ 108 milliards de dollars, soit 92,5 milliards d'euros, en 2011. Un investissement de 1 000 dollars, soit environ 856 euros, au début de son mandat vaudrait aujourd’hui près de 28 000 dollars, soit environ 24 000 euros, dividendes réinvestis inclus, selon les données de Yahoo Finance.
Tim Cook a transformé la machine à produits de Steve Jobs en un moteur de revenus plus large. Les services d’Apple sont devenus une activité annuelle de 109 milliards de dollars, soit environ 93 milliards d'euros, portée par un parc de 2,5 milliards d’appareils actifs, l’Apple Watch, les AirPods et la migration des Mac vers la puce Apple Silicon. Le groupe a par ailleurs consacré plus de 880 milliards de dollars, soit environ 754 milliards d'euros, au rachat de ses propres actions depuis 2012. Lors de l’assemblée générale de Berkshire Hathaway en 2026, Warren Buffett a rappelé que les 35 milliards de dollars investis à l’origine dans Apple, soit environ 30 milliards d'euros, avaient atteint près de 185 milliards de dollars avant impôts, soit environ 158 milliards d'’euros.
Le dirigeant sortant a déclaré, lors de sa dernière conférence sur les résultats, que le traitement embarqué est un « atout concurrentiel majeur », tout en reconnaissant une hausse des dépenses liées à l’intelligence artificielle. Il a ajouté que la transition vers John Ternus avançait « sans accroc » et qu’il n’avait « jamais été aussi optimiste ».

articles.title: Botão anti-IA do LinkedIn é avaliado positivamente • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Botão anti-IA do LinkedIn é avaliado positivamente
Após o recurso registrar mais de 1 milhão de acionamentos, plataforma escondeu publicações genéricas e passou a emitir alertas aos criadores afetados.
O LinkedIn anunciou que conseguiu diminuir em 40% as visualizações de publicações de baixa qualidade geradas por inteligência artificial. A queda drástica ocorre poucas semanas após a rede social liberar um botão de denúncia para esse tipo de material. O objetivo é limpar o feed, penalizar conteúdos que não agregam valor e, a partir de agora, notificar os autores das postagens reportadas pelo público.
O diretor de produtos do LinkedIn, Hari Srinivasan, confirmou que os membros já estão visualizando uma quantidade muito menor de textos robotizados. A nova funcionalidade de moderação, apelidada como “botão contra lixo de IA” (ou “AI slop”, no jargão do setor de tecnologia), teve uma adoção rápida: já foi acionada mais de 1 milhão de vezes desde o lançamento.
Apesar do sucesso, a empresa mantém reservas sobre como processa as denúncias geradas pelos usuários para rebaixar o que considera “conteúdo de baixa qualidade”. Para evitar abusos ou perseguições, foram criados mecanismos que impedem que uma onda de feedbacks negativos seja utilizada para atacar ou silenciar outros membros injustamente.
Isso significa que apenas receber cliques no botão de denúncia não garante que uma postagem será ocultada caso o sistema interno não sustente a suspeita de uso inadequado de IA. A plataforma também realizou ajustes de algoritmo e passou a identificar e reduzir o alcance de publicações que abusam de clichês textuais já reconhecidos como assinaturas de sistemas de IA generativa – como posts que estruturam argumentos em fórmulas previsíveis, como o formato “não é sobre X, é sobre Y”.
A rede da Microsoft também introduziu um sistema de transparência. Os usuários vão receber um alerta sempre que uma publicação sua for denunciada por terceiros como “possível texto de inteligência artificial genérico”. Esse aviso não será exibido publicamente e ficará restrito ao painel de “análise de publicações” do aplicativo.
Um estudo recente conduzido pela empresa de detecção de IA Pangram estimou que mais de 40% das publicações longas no LinkedIn provavelmente foram criadas por inteligência artificial. Esse volume sem precedentes não ocorreu por acaso. O próprio aplicativo adotava uma postura de incentivo ao uso da tecnologia, incluindo até um botão na interface de criação que sugeria “aprimorar” publicações utilizando algoritmos de escrita.
No entanto, essa “facilidade” acabou descaracterizando a plataforma. Reconhecendo o impacto negativo na experiência dos usuários, a empresa optou por remover completamente o recurso assim que lançou a atual ferramenta de denúncia.

articles.title: Google and the UK government are looking to remove aircraft contrails using AI
articles.text:
Google and the UK government are looking to remove aircraft contrails using AI
Operation Blue Skies looks to tidy up the sky
- A £5 million trial is examining whether AI can assist in the reduction or removal of contrails from aircraft
- Contrails appear when the exhaust from aircraft engines hits the cold, high-altitude air, which creates ice crystals
- Also known as vapour trails, contrails are believed to contribute to climate change
Google, the Met Office, and the UK Government are cooperating with NATS (formerly National Air Traffic Services) and the University of Cambridge and Imperial College London on Operation Blue Skies, which aims to reduce or remove contrails from aircraft traveling from Europe to the USA and Canada.
Targeting the North Atlantic, the project will explore the possibility of diverting craft around areas of particularly cold air, thereby reducing contrails (also known as vapour trails) and avoiding their impact on the climate.
Google’s contribution will include the use of AI to learn from the gathered data and build a picture of how contrails are formed over the North Atlantic.
Landmark consortium
The organizations collaborating on this research project each play their own role.
While Google is providing AI models, machine learning, and satellite imaging (pro bono, at an estimated £1.4 million value), NATS oversees airspace and safety assessments, and the educational institutions evaluate outcomes and independently verify the data and results. Meanwhile, the Met Office is developing new contrail forecasting, along with meteorology.
Also involved is the website Contrails.org, which is designing trial parameters and handling forecast assessments.
Funding for the project is coming from the UK government’s Department for Transport, bringing together the Aerospace Technology Institute (ATI), the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) and Innovate UK under its ATI Programme.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Operation Blue Skies aims to demonstrate that solving the challenge of contrails is operationally practical,” says Google, “providing a validated blueprint for how our airspaces can be managed to drastically reduce aviation's climate impact.”
Operation Blue Skies is not the only such project in operation (Google previously worked with American Airlines on a similar basis), but it is the first to be backed by government funding.
33% of aviation climate warming
The project will focus on the eastern half of the North Atlantic corridor, the Shanwick Oceanic zone, where around 5% of global contrail warming occurs. Running for 30 months, two operational trials running four months each will observe 10,000 flights, with some given slight deviations to reduce travel “through contrail-sensitive airspace.”
If successful, findings from the Blue Skies Project could become standard operational procedure during flights. Dr. Paul Hodgson, Google's technical lead for the operation, told the BBC, "We think that contrail warming is responsible for something like a third of all aviation climate warming. The CO2 penalty is in the order of less than 1%, compared to the contrail cost, which is of a similar order of magnitude to all of the CO2 of aviation."
Operation Blue Skies will commence formal trials over the winter of 2026-2027, with the second trial period during the winter of 2027-2028.

articles.title: Studie überrascht: Menschen bewerten KI-Geschichten besser als menschliche Storys
articles.text:
„Einfacher zu lesen“: Warum KI-Geschichten als fesselnder empfunden werden
Auf Linkedin haben KI-generierte Karrieretipps oder Erfolgsgeschichten offenbar dermaßen die Überhand gewonnen, dass die Karriereplattform jetzt mit einer neuen Meldefunktion dagegen vorgeht. 41 Prozent der untersuchten längeren Beiträge (ab 250 Wörtern) wurden von dem KI-Analysetool Pangram als vollständig KI-generiert eingestuft.
KI-generierte Geschichten beliebter
Nutzer:innen fühlten sich offenbar zunehmend genervt von dem „AI-Slop“, wie zahlreiche Beschwerdebeiträge zeigen. Nicht so ganz ins Bild passen da die Ergebnisse einer Studie der Villanova University im US-Bundesstaat Pennsylvania. Demnach mochten die Teilnehmer:innen die KI-generierten Geschichten lieber als die zum Vergleich vorgelegten Storys von Menschen.
Konkret bekamen die Studienteilnehmer:innen eine von sechs Kurzgeschichten zum Lesen vorgelegt, von denen je drei von KI beziehungsweise von Menschen geschrieben worden waren. Die behandelten Themen waren ähnlich. Die Teilnehmer:innen erfuhren, ob der jeweilige Text KI-generiert war oder nicht. Allerdings machten die Forscher:innen hier hin und wieder absichtlich falsche Angaben.
Fesselnder und qualitativ hochwertiger?
Im Ergebnis zeigte sich, dass jene, die KI-generierte Storys lasen, diese als fesselnder und qualitativ hochwertiger empfanden. Die Forscher:innen gehen davon aus, dass diese Geschichten einfacher zu lesen und zu verstehen sind als jene, die von Menschen geschrieben wurden.
Interessant war, dass Teilnehmer:innen Storys eine bessere Bewertung gaben, wenn sie glaubten, dass diese von Menschen stammten. „KI-Systeme können schon Kurzgeschichten generieren, die mindestens so gut – wenn nicht sogar besser – sind als von Menschen geschriebene Geschichten“, betonte die Psychologin Deena Skolnick Weisberg von der Villanova University, eine der Hauptautor:innen der Studie.
Ist es also an der Zeit, unsere Einschätzung zu den Fähigkeiten von KI entsprechend anzupassen, wie Weisberg vorschlägt? Luke Kennard, Professor für Film und kreatives Schreiben an der University of Birmingham, ist da ganz anderer Meinung. Die Menschen tendierten dazu, KI zu personifizieren und sie sich als eine Art Roboter mit gutartigem Gesicht vorzustellen.
Riesige Datenbank mit gestohlenen Texten
Stattdessen, so Kennard gegenüber dem Guardian, handele es sich dabei nur um Code, der auf einer „riesigen Datenbank mit gestohlenem Text“ basiere. Natürlich bringe die KI unterhaltsame Texte zustande. Es wäre aber auch peinlich, so Kennard, wenn sie das nicht könne – angesichts des Trainings mit menschlicher Arbeit aus einigen Jahrtausenden.
Auch Weisberg, die selbst Schriftstellerin ist, betont derweil, dass das Schreiben nicht der KI überlassen werden sollte. „Menschen schreiben, um sich kreativ auszudrücken, sich selbst herauszufordern oder ihre Erfahrungen zu verarbeiten“, so Weisberg. Daran ändere die Tatsache, dass KI menschenähnliche Geschichten generieren könne, nichts. Man müsse sich allerdings vermehrt auf KI-generierte Romane einstellen.

articles.title: Camping-car et Google Maps : l’erreur classique qui se termine presque toujours en piège
articles.text:
Camping-car et Google Maps : l’erreur classique qui se termine presque toujours en piège
Google Maps excelle à préparer un voyage, lire le trafic et repérer une destination. Il n’offre en revanche aucun profil camping-car : ni hauteur, ni largeur, ni longueur, ni poids. Pour éviter les routes inadaptées, il lui faut un binôme, un GPS qui tient vraiment compte du gabarit.
La route se rétrécit, les rétroviseurs frôlent les murs de pierre et une file de voitures commence à s’impatienter derrière le camping-car. Impossible d’avancer sereinement, encore moins de faire demi-tour avec sept mètres de cellule. Le GPS affiche pourtant tranquillement : "Continuez tout droit". La scène se répète chaque été, sur les mêmes routes. Elle vient toujours du même geste : confier à une application généraliste une décision qu’elle ne sait pas prendre, celle de choisir un itinéraire adapté aux dimensions et au poids d’un gros véhicule.
Le malentendu de départ : Google Maps ne connaît pas le gabarit
Disons-le clairement. Google Maps ne propose aucun profil camping-car, caravane ou poids lourd, donc aucun champ pour saisir la hauteur, la largeur, la longueur, le poids total ou la charge à l’essieu. Voiture, deux-roues, transports en commun, vélo, marche : voilà ses modes d’itinéraire. Un camping-car de 3,5 tonnes y est traité exactement comme une berline, ce qui suffit à expliquer pourquoi l’application vous envoie parfois dans une rue de village où aucun véhicule de plus de deux mètres cinquante n’a rien à faire.
Conséquence directe : aucune garantie d’éviter les ponts bas, les tunnels limités, les routes étroites, les restrictions de tonnage ou les interdictions locales. L’application affiche bien certaines restrictions présentes dans ses données. Elle ne les croise pas avec vos mesures.
Deuxième confusion, très répandue : renseigner un moteur diesel n’active pas un mode camping-car. Ce paramètre alimente le calcul des itinéraires économes en carburant, là où la fonction existe, et oriente le choix d’un trajet selon son efficacité énergétique. Il ne dit rien de votre hauteur sous barre, et le mot "camping-car" n’apparaît nulle part dans ce réglage, ce qui devrait suffire à lever le doute.
Troisième idée à écarter : le mode hors connexion. Télécharger une zone permet de consulter la carte et de se faire guider sans données mobiles. Rien de plus. Aucune gestion du gabarit à l’horizon.
Là où Google Maps reste très utile
Faut-il le désinstaller ? Surtout pas. Google Maps reste un excellent outil de préparation et de contrôle, à une condition : ne rien lui demander qui ressemble à du routage spécialisé. Tracer les grandes étapes, comparer des axes, estimer les durées, localiser commerces, stations-service, parkings et points d’intérêt, retrouver tout ça sur smartphone pendant le voyage. Voilà son terrain.
Son trafic en temps réel vaut de l’or pour anticiper ralentissements, accidents et fermetures sur les grands axes. Il fait aussi un excellent second avis face à un GPS spécialisé : quand un bouchon se forme sur l’itinéraire prévu, il montre l’ampleur du problème et les contournements possibles. Attention quand même. Une déviation proposée par Google Maps se vérifie avant d’être suivie : rien ne garantit qu’elle passe avec sept mètres de cellule.
Street View est l’autre atout, quand les images existent et qu’elles sont assez récentes. Avant de viser une aire, un village ou une route secondaire, on y observe l’entrée d’un parking, un porche, la largeur apparente d’une rue, un virage serré, une barrière de hauteur. Ce repérage visuel ne remplace évidemment ni la signalisation ni un GPS à gabarit. En revanche, dix minutes passées à remonter virtuellement la rue d’accès d’une aire avant de s’y engager font gagner des demi-tours, et parfois davantage.
Un détail pratique, pour finir sur ce point : les itinéraires enregistrés, les favoris et les options disponibles ne sont pas identiques entre l’application mobile et la version Web. Vérifiez sur le support que vous emporterez, avant le départ.
La vraie astuce : associer deux outils
Deux outils, deux rôles. Google Maps, ou Waze, pour la vision générale, le trafic et la recherche de lieux. Un GPS spécialisé pour le routage. Lui seul connaît vos mesures. Ces solutions réclament au minimum la hauteur, la largeur et le poids, les plus complètes ajoutant la longueur, la charge à l’essieu et la vitesse maximale. Prenez ces mesures une fois, sérieusement, véhicule chargé et accessoires de toit en place : c’est le socle de tout le reste, et une erreur de dix centimètres se paie devant un porche.
Sygic GPS Truck & Caravan propose des profils pour véhicules de grand gabarit et des cartes hors ligne. Ses licences se déclinent selon les options et les plateformes, sans tarif unique : le prix se lit dans l’application ou sur la boutique, au moment de l’achat.
TomTom décline des profils Camping-car et Caravane sur ses appareils et services compatibles. Selon le produit, les réglages couvrent la longueur, la hauteur, la largeur, le poids total, la charge à l’essieu et la vitesse maximale. Vérifiez avant tout achat que le modèle visé embarque bien le profil recherché. Les fonctions diffèrent entre appareils dédiés et applications, y compris chez un même constructeur.
Côté smartphone, Gabary est une application française pensée pour les camping-cars et les vans. On y renseigne le gabarit, elle annonce des itinéraires conçus pour éviter ponts bas, limitations et routes étroites. Son offre Premium fonctionne par abonnement, avec des tarifs et une couverture géographique qui évoluent régulièrement.
Magic Earth embarque une navigation poids lourd fondée sur les dimensions, le poids total, la charge à l’essieu et la vitesse maximale. Comme partout ici, les fonctions et leurs conditions d’accès évoluent : ouvrez l’application avant de préparer un grand voyage, pas après.
Pour l’étape du soir, Park4Night ou Campercontact complètent le dispositif. Ils repèrent aires, campings et stationnements, avec des retours d’utilisateurs qui valent souvent mieux qu’une fiche officielle sur l’état réel d’un emplacement. Ils ne conduisent pas jusque-là : le trajet final reste l’affaire du GPS à gabarit, que certains de ces services savent d’ailleurs ouvrir directement sur la destination choisie.
Aucun GPS n’est infaillible. Les bases de données comportent des trous, les restrictions changent d’une saison à l’autre, et un panneau posé la semaine dernière ne figure dans aucune carte. D’où la règle qui vaut pour toutes les solutions citées, quel que soit leur prix : ce que vous voyez par le pare-brise l’emporte sur ce qu’annonce l’écran. Toujours.

articles.title: No sabía que necesitaba una cámara de vigilancia hasta que probé la Ring Spotlight. Luego descubrí que es un Caballo de Troya
articles.text:
Una de las cosas que me conquistaron del piso que compré hace unos meses fue que tiene dos patios que me vienen de cine para hacer pinitos en mi poco conocida labor de agricultora, tomar el sol, tender y que mis perras yazcan a la fresca.
Lo no tan bueno es que igual que algún repartidor me deja los paquetes tirándolos por la valla o hasta metiendo el brazo, a cualquier amigo de lo ajeno no debería costarle demasiado saltar la verja y acceder. Yo misma me he planteado hacerlo ante un olvido de llaves. Hacía tiempo que tenía en mente comprar una cámara de vigilancia, así que cuando surgió la oportunidad de probar esta Ring Spotlight Camera, no me lo pensé dos veces.Esta ha sido mi experiencia.
✅ Cómpralo si...
- Quieres una cámara fácil de usar y de instalar.
- Vídeo de calidad de día y de noche,
- Tu ecosistema es el de Amazon Alexa.
❌ No lo compres si...
- Hay muchas funciones que requieren de suscripción.
- Carece de almacenamiento en local.
- No es compatible con Google Assistant o Apple HomeKit.
Lo esencial en 30 segundos
Esta es una cámara de vigilancia inalámbrica que puedes instalar tanto en exteriores como en interiores, si bien por su diseño y funciones donde más conveniente resulta es fuera de casa. Configurarla en la app e instalarla en el patio nos llevó menos de 10 minutos y no hizo falta mucha historia más allá de un buen taladro para hacer los agujeros en la pared.
Poner en marcha la app también fue coser y cantar: crearse una cuenta, que da 30 días de suscripción gratis a las funciones premium. Más adelante profundizaremos en lo que viene gratis y lo que no, pero ya os adelanto algo: si solo lo quieres para vigilar en el momento qué pasa en ese lugar donde la has instalado y ahuyentar a posibles malhechores, cumple sin pagar ni un euro. Eso sí, que no tenga la posibilidad de almacenamiento en local es un hándicap que pesa.
La aplicación es extremadamente intuitiva y tiene todo lo necesario para controlar la zona donde de vigilancia, avisos en caso de que algo se mueva cerca y algunos extra útiles para la seguridad como unos focos sorprendentemente potentes para su tamaño, comunicación bidireccional y hasta una sirena.
Ring Cámara con luces (Spotlight Cam), con batería(última generación),Retinal 2K,zoom mejorado de 6 aumentos, focos activados por movimiento, prueba gratuita de 30 días del plan de suscripción a Ring
Nuestra experiencia con el Ring Spotlight Camera
Un diseño funcional. No es la cámara más discreta y compacta del mundo, pero tiene una construcción robusta y práctica: escoltando a la cámara están dos columnas donde se integran los LEDs en el frontal, en la parte inferior tiene una tapa para abrir y colocar al menos una batería (solo viene una, pero le caben dos) y en la trasera dos orificios para elegir dónde incrustar el soporte, que es el que fijaremos en la pared y rotaremos con la rótula que integra según convenga. En cuanto a cómo aguanta las inclemencias del tiempo, Amazon se limita a decir: "resistente a la intemperie", lo que es demasiado vago. De momento, lleva un mes soportando la chicharrina diurna y la humedad nocturna de un pueblo de Navarra sin problema.
Alto, no se mueva. Además de la cámara y los LED de iluminación, el panel frontal integra un par de micrófonos, un sensor de movimiento PIR, un sensor de luz ambiental, un LED de estado y un altavoz. Así, cuando la cámara está grabando, el LED se ilumina en azul, pero si tiene problemas pasa a rojo. Una vez configuradas las opciones y la sensibilidad, si detecta movimiento en la zona de vigilancia, da el aviso en la app y tienes la opción de que se enciendan los LED para pillar in fraganti y hasta de que suene una sirena. Es decir, que la cámara informa y disuade a potenciales maleantes porque el combo de luz y sirena da mucho el cante.
Vídeos resultones y cumplidores. No es una cámara 4K, pero para este escenario tampoco le hace falta. Durante el día toma vídeos en color y una calidad decente más que suficiente para reconocer detalles de un rostro incluso aunque haya poca luz y haciendo zoom. Eso sí, los colores tienden a ser apagados. De noche, la visión nocturna entrega imágenes en blanco y negro de alto contraste. Si además configuras los LED para que se enciendan, pues mejor que mejor. Como el campo de visión es tan amplio, cubre bien bastante área (la puerta de mi patio y el dormitorio), por lo que hay que tener cuidado para no grabar zonas privadas y tener problemas con los vecinos (y la ley).
Una app intuitiva. Probablemente lo que más me ha gustado es lo fácil que es de usar la aplicación. Entras y ves las cámaras que tienes, eliges la que te interesa ver y una vez dentro, puedes ver en directo lo que está pasando, además de encender las luces, poner la alarma o escuchar y hablar. Si tocas en el engranaje accedes a la configuración, lo que permite ajustar cosas como que se encienda la luz o no o variar la sensibilidad. Todo intuitivo, claro y con consejos para que cumpla bien con sus objetivos. Un ejemplo: cuando la configuré inicialmente, la app me molestaba demasiado cada vez que pasaban las perras cerca, pero logré solucionarlo con un ajuste de la sensibilidad. Todo te llega al móvil, pero si tienes un altavoz de Amazon, también puedes controlarlo desde allí (y hasta verlo).
Qué viene gratis y qué no. En mis semanas de uso para la review me ha tocado disfrutar de esos 30 días gratis de prueba, lo que implica poder disfrutar de todas sus funciones, algunas de ellas tan importantes como el almacenamiento en la nube de hasta 180 días o poder buscar clips específicos con IA. Si no pagas suscripción, la cámara funciona exclusivamente como un dispositivo de monitorización en tiempo real activo: te avisa y tu vas a la app y controlas qué pasa, pero no guarda ni graba ningún fragmento de video en la nube y no tiene posibilidad de meterle un USB o SD para grabar sin depender de sus servidores.
Pase por caja, por favor. Lo anterior puede ser suficiente en algunos casos, pero a título personal le faltan algunas funciones que me resultan esenciales, lo que me obligaría a pagar al menos por el plan Basic (3,99 euros/mes o 39,99 euros/año), cubre un solo dispositivo y historial de vídeo de hasta 180 días, alertas de personas/paquetes y vista previa de eventos. El modo estándar (9,99 euros/mes o 99,99 euros/año) cubre todos los dispositivos de tu vivienda y añade vídeo en directo ampliado, llamadas de timbre, resumen diario de eventos y las funciones de Ring Alarm. El Premium (19,99 euros/mes o 199,99 euros/año) incluye todo lo del Estándar más funciones avanzadas como grabación ininterrumpida, vídeo en directo continuo, búsqueda inteligente y reconocimiento de rostros.
Ficha técnica del Ring Spotlight Camera
|  | Ring Spotlight Camera | 
|---|---|
| Dimensiones | 123 mm x 80 mm x 83 mm | 
| Vídeo | 2K (2560 x 1440) Campo de visión: 140° en horizontal, 85° en vertical Hasta 6 aumentos | 
| Funciones | Sirena Iluminación: focos de 550 lúmenes Detección de movimiento avanzada con zonas de movimiento personalizables Comunicación bidireccional | 
| CONECTIVIDAD | Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz Compatible con Alexa | 
| Alimentación | Batería recargable (1 incluida, con capacidad para 2). Opción de usar con panel solar (a la venta por separado) | 
| COndiciones Funcionamiento | De -20 °C a 50 °C, resistente a la intemperie | 
| Qué hay en la caja | Cámara, soporte, piezas de instalación (cables y tacos), cable de carga micro USB, manuales | 
| Precio | 169 euros | 
Ring Spotlight Camera, la opinión de Xataka
Esta Ring Spotlight Camera es una cámara que lo pone muy fácil: está bien construida, su instalación es coser y cantar, la aplicación funciona con soltura y está cuidada al detalle, y en términos de seguridad ofrece mucho más que el simple visionado. Si además tenemos en cuenta que puedes escalar la vigilancia añadiendo más dispositivos de Ring (hay opciones para casi cualquier escenario y presupuesto) y supervisarlo todo desde la app, el resultado es, objetivamente, un sistema que da mucho por un precio atractivo.
Exactamente igual que otros productos de la casa de Amazon, porque esa es precisamente su estrategia: equipos con buena relación calidad-precio en diseño, materiales o funciones, pero con una letra pequeña que te mete de lleno en su ecosistema. En este caso, además, lo hace con un peaje en forma de suscripción: algunos extras son prescindibles, pero para aprovechar ciertas funciones básicas hay que pasar por caja.
¿Lo recomiendo?
Depende de lo que busques. Esta cámara de vigilancia es buena, bonita y relativamente barata para lo que ofrece. Eso sí, ten en cuenta que probablemente acabes pagando más, a menos que te conformes con que te avise cuando detecte algo extraño y puedas mirar en ese preciso momento (si estás en el cine y no puedes hacerlo, te lo pierdes).
Y si hay que pagar de más, entonces toca hacer números para ver si compensa. Ahora bien, si ya formas parte del ecosistema Amazon y/o no te importa asumir una suscripción, es una opción magnífica.
Este dispositivo ha sido cedido para prueba por parte de Ring. Puedes consultar cómo hacemos las reviews en Xataka y nuestra política de relaciones con empresas.
